task_1.title: Support dependency-only projects with Poetry non-package mode
task_1.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adds an opt-in non-package mode for projects that use Poetry only for dependency management. This mode relaxes package metadata requirements, skips installation of the root project during install, and blocks build and publish workflows that only apply to packages.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects using Poetry only for dependency management can opt out of package semantics, so they are not required to provide package metadata, do not install the root project during dependency installation, and cannot accidentally run packaging-only workflows.

expectation.grounded: Poetry must support the tool.poetry setting package-mode = false as an explicit non-package mode. When package-mode is false, metadata such as the project name and version are not required, poetry install must behave like --no-root for the current project, and poetry build and poetry publish must fail with a non-zero result instead of attempting packaging operations. The default package mode must continue to require package metadata.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to configure Poetry for dependency management only. In that mode, dependency installation should still work, the local project itself should not be installed, and packaging commands should be unavailable because the project is not being treated as a distributable package.

constraints.grounded: Package mode remains the default behavior. Non-package mode must not silently build or publish artifacts, and dependency installation in non-package mode must complete without installing the root project. Projects that stay in package mode must continue to be validated as packages, including required metadata expectations.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability must be opt-in, preserve existing package-oriented behavior by default, and only relax rules that are irrelevant for dependency-only workflows.

behavior: poetry install skips installation of the current project when non-package mode is active, even if --no-root is not provided.
poetry build is rejected in non-package mode and returns a failure status instead of starting a package build.
poetry publish is rejected in non-package mode and returns a failure status instead of attempting publication.

When installation of the current project fails in package mode, the user-facing warning now directs dependency-only users toward either --no-root or non-package mode rather than treating the situation as a successful root install.
acceptance_criteria: When a project sets tool.poetry.package-mode = false, it should be valid to use Poetry without declaring package metadata such as name and version.
When poetry install runs for a project in non-package mode, it should install dependencies without installing the root project.
When poetry build is invoked for a project in non-package mode, it should fail clearly and should not create package artifacts.
When poetry publish is invoked for a project in non-package mode, it should fail clearly and should not attempt to publish artifacts.
When a project remains in the default package mode, missing required package metadata should still be treated as invalid configuration.

task_3.title: Enable lazy wheel metadata retrieval for dependency resolution
task_3.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adds a default-on `solver.lazy-wheel` setting so dependency resolution can prefer published metadata or fetch only wheel metadata over HTTP instead of downloading entire wheel files. The resolver must preserve correctness by validating metadata when hashes are available and by falling back to normal archive inspection when repositories do not support reliable range requests.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution reduces unnecessary wheel downloads by default while still resolving package metadata correctly across repositories that expose metadata directly, support HTTP byte ranges, or require full archive downloads.

expectation.grounded: Expose a boolean Poetry config key `solver.lazy-wheel` with default `true`. During repository inspection, prefer core metadata exposed by a distribution link when available; otherwise, when inspecting a wheel and `solver.lazy-wheel` is enabled, retrieve the wheel's `METADATA` using HTTP range requests instead of downloading the full wheel. If range access, metadata retrieval, or metadata validation cannot be completed, fall back to normal wheel or sdist inspection and continue producing the same package metadata fields used for resolution, including dependency requirements and Python version constraints.
expectation.conceptual: Poetry should minimize network transfer during dependency resolution by using published metadata when possible and by lazily reading only the metadata portion of remote wheels when needed. This optimization should be enabled by default, configurable by the user, and transparent: unsupported or unreliable repositories should still resolve successfully through the existing full-download path.

constraints.grounded: Disabling `solver.lazy-wheel` must skip lazy wheel inspection. Metadata sidecars must be ignored if they cannot be retrieved or if their advertised hashes do not validate. Range-request behavior must tolerate servers that do not support byte ranges, do not support negative ranges, return full content instead of partial content, or behave inconsistently across files on the same domain, without treating lazy retrieval failures as package metadata failures when a normal download can still succeed.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization must never change the resolved metadata contract or make repository compatibility worse. Correctness and compatibility take precedence over bandwidth savings, and users must be able to turn the optimization off to restore eager downloads.

behavior: Adds a new boolean configuration option, `solver.lazy-wheel`, defaulting to enabled.
Repository inspection now consumes published core metadata for a distribution link when that metadata is present and valid, instead of forcing archive inspection.
When direct metadata is unavailable and lazy wheel mode is enabled, wheel inspection fetches only the remote wheel `METADATA` via HTTP byte-range requests.

If a server or domain cannot satisfy the required range-request behavior, inspection falls back to HEAD and/or full archive download paths rather than failing solely because lazy access is unsupported.

Range-request capability is tracked per domain so compatible repositories can keep using lazy wheel retrieval, while mixed or previously misdetected support can still recover to the lazy path for later artifacts.
Metadata extracted from sidecars or lazy wheel access feeds the same package information fields used by dependency resolution, including name, version, summary, dependencies, and Python requirements.
acceptance_criteria: When configuration is read or set, `solver.lazy-wheel` should be available as a boolean option and should default to enabled when unset.

When a repository exposes distribution metadata directly, resolving a package should use that metadata without requiring a full wheel download, and invalid metadata hashes should cause Poetry to ignore that metadata and fall back to artifact inspection.

When `solver.lazy-wheel` is enabled and a repository supports the necessary HTTP range requests, resolving a package from a wheel should succeed by reading the wheel metadata without downloading the entire wheel archive.

When a repository does not support byte ranges, does not support negative range requests, or returns incompatible range responses, resolving the same package should still succeed through fallback archive inspection.
When `solver.lazy-wheel` is set to `false`, Poetry should use the non-lazy archive inspection path instead of ranged wheel metadata retrieval.

When metadata is obtained from a sidecar file, a ranged wheel read, or a full archive download, the resulting resolution behavior should reflect the same declared dependencies and Python version constraints.

task_2.title: Support PEP 658 metadata from simple package indexes
task_2.description: The update allows the client to consume repository-provided core metadata from simple package indexes, including PyPI fallback paths, so package dependencies and related metadata can be resolved without downloading full distribution archives when metadata sidecars are available. It also preserves compatibility by supporting current and legacy metadata markers, validating advertised metadata hashes, and falling back to archive inspection when sidecar metadata cannot be trusted or retrieved.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that packages published on PEP 503 simple repositories that expose PEP 658 core metadata can be resolved without downloading the full wheel or source distribution, while still returning correct dependency metadata, Python version constraints, summary information, and release file data when sidecar metadata is missing, invalid, or unavailable.

expectation.grounded: `HTTPRepository` and `PyPiRepository` should prefer repository-advertised core metadata for supported distribution `Link`s before inspecting wheel or sdist archives. Link parsing should recognize both the current `core-metadata` and `data-core-metadata` markers and the legacy `dist-info-metadata` and `data-dist-info-metadata` markers, with the current marker taking precedence when both are present. When a link exposes metadata, the client should fetch the linked `.metadata` resource, parse it into `PackageInfo`, and populate observable package fields such as `summary`, `requires_dist`, and `requires_python`. If advertised metadata hashes are present, the fetched metadata should be verified against the strongest supported advertised hash and ignored on mismatch. If metadata retrieval fails or is rejected, package inspection should fall back to the existing wheel, sdist, and lazy-wheel or range-request paths instead of failing solely because sidecar metadata could not be used.
expectation.conceptual: When a package index publishes sidecar core metadata for a release file, the client should use that metadata directly to resolve package information instead of requiring a full archive download. This should work with both current and older metadata markers used by simple indexes. If the sidecar cannot be fetched or does not validate, users should still get the same resolved package information through the normal archive inspection fallback.

constraints.grounded: Metadata sidecars are an optimization and compatibility path, not a hard dependency. Existing distribution selection behavior should remain intact, including preferring wheels over sdists, honoring yanked-file filtering, and preserving lazy-wheel behavior for wheel inspection. Hash handling should continue to prefer the strongest available distribution hash information, and metadata validation failures should degrade to warnings and fallback inspection rather than corrupting resolved package metadata.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must improve repository compatibility and reduce unnecessary downloads without changing successful resolution outcomes for repositories that already worked. Repositories that do not provide usable sidecar metadata should continue to behave as before, and invalid sidecar metadata must not become the source of truth.

behavior: Simple repository HTML and JSON link parsing recognizes repository-advertised core metadata indicators for distribution files, including both current and legacy marker names.
When a distribution link advertises sidecar metadata, package metadata is derived from the fetched core metadata instead of first downloading and inspecting the full wheel or sdist archive.
Advertised metadata hashes are checked using the strongest supported available hash; if the fetched metadata does not match, the sidecar is ignored and archive-based inspection is used.
HTTP failures while fetching sidecar metadata do not immediately break package inspection; the client falls back to normal wheel or sdist introspection.
PyPI fallback for releases whose JSON metadata lacks dependency information consults simple-index links, allowing PEP 658 metadata to supply dependency and Python requirement data.
Wheel-selection preferences remain in effect when choosing which release file to inspect, but the chosen file's sidecar metadata may satisfy the inspection without a full download.
acceptance_criteria: When a simple repository exposes `core-metadata` or legacy `dist-info-metadata` for a supported release file, resolving that release should populate dependency metadata, summary, and Python constraints from the sidecar metadata without requiring a full archive download.
When both current and legacy metadata markers are present for the same release file, the current `core-metadata` marker should determine sidecar availability and hash data.

When sidecar metadata is advertised with a hash and the fetched content does not match that hash, the client should ignore the sidecar metadata and obtain package metadata through normal archive inspection instead.

When sidecar metadata retrieval returns an HTTP error or the repository does not expose sidecar metadata, package resolution should continue through the existing archive-inspection path rather than failing solely because the sidecar could not be used.

When PyPI JSON release data omits dependency metadata but the corresponding simple index exposes usable sidecar metadata, the resolved package should still include dependency and Python requirement information.

When a repository release offers multiple supported files, the existing file-preference rules should still determine which candidate metadata source is used, with sidecar metadata only changing how metadata is obtained for that candidate.

task_5.title: Validate dependency source references during `poetry check`
task_5.description: Poetry 1.8.0 strengthens `poetry check` so validation now fails when dependencies reference package sources that are not declared by the project. The check applies across main dependencies, dependency groups, and list-style dependency declarations, giving users earlier feedback about misconfigured source usage.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry check` reports an error whenever any dependency references a package source that is not declared in the project's configured sources, including dependencies defined in the main dependency section, dependency groups, and alternative or list-based declarations.

expectation.grounded: `poetry check` should collect source names declared in the project's `source` configuration and validate every dependency-level `source` reference found in top-level `dependencies` and in each entry under dependency groups. The validation should inspect both single dependency tables and list-based dependency declarations, and it should add a check error for each distinct referenced source name that is not declared.
expectation.conceptual: Running `poetry check` should catch undefined dependency source references up front. If a dependency points to a repository or source name the project has not declared, the command should fail validation and surface that configuration problem to the user.

constraints.grounded: Only undefined source references should be rejected. Dependencies that omit a `source` field should remain unaffected, declared source names should not raise errors, and the validation should not introduce a separate failure mode merely because a dependency may appear with different valid sources across declarations.
constraints.conceptual: The new validation should stay narrow and non-disruptive: it should flag only truly unknown source names, while leaving valid dependency configurations unchanged.

behavior: `poetry check` now performs dependency source validation as part of its normal error collection.
Dependency source validation covers both the main dependency table and dependency groups.
Dependency entries expressed as multiple alternative declarations are inspected for `source` references in each alternative.
Each distinct dependency source name that is referenced but not declared by the project is surfaced as a validation error once.
acceptance_criteria: When a project has a dependency whose `source` references a name that is not declared in the project's configured sources, `poetry check` should report that as an error.
When undefined source references appear in dependency groups, `poetry check` should report them the same way as top-level dependency errors.
When a dependency is declared using multiple alternatives and one or more alternatives reference undefined sources, `poetry check` should report those undefined source names as errors.
When all dependency `source` references match declared project sources, this validation should not add any new errors.
When the same undefined source name is referenced by multiple dependency declarations, `poetry check` should still surface that source as a validation problem.

task_4.title: Treat package extras as immutable for shallow-copy resolution
task_4.description: Poetry 1.8.0 changes dependency resolution to rely on shallow package copies for better performance. To keep resolution correct, package extras and duplicate-dependency overrides must behave as immutable package state when packages are reconstructed from metadata, loaded from lock data, and branched during solving.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution can use shallow package copies without changing how extras and duplicate conditional dependencies are interpreted, including when package data comes from published metadata or an existing lock file.

expectation.grounded: Packages reconstructed from `PackageInfo` metadata or `Locker` lock data should build `Package.extras` as a complete mapping before resolution proceeds, and `Provider` should read and record dependency overrides against the resolved `Package` instance so shallow-cloned package variants keep isolated extras and override state.
expectation.conceptual: The 1.8.0 upgrade should make dependency resolution faster while preserving the same observable extras behavior. Package variants created during solving must not share mutable optional-dependency or override state with each other.

constraints.grounded: Do not change which dependencies are base requirements versus extra-scoped requirements, do not alter the effective lock data for equivalent dependency inputs, and do not let an override selected for one resolved package variant apply to a different package or extra selection.
constraints.conceptual: Keep dependency and extras semantics stable while improving performance. Independent resolution branches must remain isolated, and lock-backed package reconstruction must behave the same as metadata-backed reconstruction.

behavior: Packages created from distribution metadata collect extra-scoped dependencies into a separate extras mapping and expose that mapping only after requirement parsing is complete.
Packages loaded from lock data rebuild their extras mapping before they are used by the resolver, so extras are treated as package state rather than incrementally mutated shared collections.
Resolver override lookup and duplicate-dependency override generation are tied to the resolved `Package` variant, including feature-enabled clones, instead of a mutable wrapper object.
Duplicate conditional requirements continue to be split into override branches, but each branch keeps its own override selection without leaking into sibling branches.
acceptance_criteria: When a package declares extra-scoped dependencies in published metadata, resolving that package should still expose those extras correctly and include those dependencies only when the relevant extra is active.

When the same package is reconstructed from an existing lock file, its extras should resolve the same way as metadata-derived package data, without missing or duplicated extra dependencies caused by shared mutable state.

When a package has duplicate dependency entries that require override splitting, the chosen override should apply only to the package variant being solved and should not affect unrelated variants or packages.

When resolving projects with extras-heavy or conditionally duplicated dependencies, the resulting dependency graph should remain behaviorally consistent with prior versions while allowing the 1.8.0 shallow-copy optimization.

task_6.title: Support archive validation with all supported hash algorithms
task_6.description: Poetry 1.8.0 expands archive hash validation and artifact matching beyond SHA-256 so installs can honor any digest algorithm supported by Python's hashlib, choose compatible distribution links using recorded hashes, and fail cleanly when no usable hash algorithm is available.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that package installation and artifact selection validate archives against recorded hashes using any digest algorithm supported by the runtime, instead of assuming SHA-256, and reject artifacts whose hashes cannot be matched or verified from the available metadata.

expectation.grounded: During installation, Poetry should validate each archive using the highest-priority hash algorithm recorded for that file that is available in Python's hashlib, including supported SHA-3, SHA-2, and other available algorithms. Artifact selection should accept a distribution link when any advertised hash matches one of the locked hashes for the package file, and repository metadata should preserve or derive a usable archive hash so locked file hashes can be matched consistently. If no usable recorded hash type exists for the archive, or if no candidate link digest matches the locked metadata, Poetry should raise a RuntimeError and avoid installing the package.
expectation.conceptual: Installing from locked or repository-provided archives should verify the downloaded file against a supported recorded digest even when that digest is not SHA-256. When multiple digests exist, the installer should use a preferred supported one, accept artifacts whose published hashes agree with the lock data, and fail clearly instead of proceeding when validation is impossible or every available digest disagrees.

constraints.grounded: Existing SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 validation behavior must continue to work. Links without published hashes may still be considered, but links with hashes must only be accepted when at least one usable digest aligns with the locked metadata. Hash choice must remain deterministic across repository lookup, archive validation, and artifact cache keying for the same file.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add support for more digest algorithms without weakening integrity checks for existing workflows. It must not broaden acceptance of mismatched archives, and the same package file should be handled consistently wherever Poetry resolves, validates, or caches it.

behavior: Archive validation during installation no longer assumes sha256; it computes the digest with the highest-priority usable algorithm recorded for the archive and compares that exact algorithm and digest pair against the known hashes.

When multiple hashes are available for the same artifact, Poetry prefers supported high-priority algorithms such as SHA-3 and SHA-2 families before falling back to other hashlib algorithms available in the runtime.

Artifact selection accepts a candidate distribution when any hash advertised by the link matches one of the locked hashes for that package file, and rejects candidates whose digests do not match the lock metadata.
For HTTP-hosted artifacts, Poetry can derive a sha256 digest to normalize matching when a directly usable locked hash is not already present in the link metadata.

If the recorded hashes for an archive use no algorithm available in the current runtime, or if all candidate link digests mismatch the locked hashes, installation aborts with a RuntimeError and the package is not installed.
acceptance_criteria: When a locked archive is recorded with a supported non-sha256 hash such as sha512, sha3_512, or md5, installing that package should validate the archive with that algorithm and proceed only if the digest matches.
When multiple hashes are recorded for the same archive, installation should succeed without requiring a sha256 entry as long as at least one supported preferred hash matches the downloaded file.

When a package index link advertises multiple hashes, dependency selection should keep the link if any advertised digest matches the locked metadata for that file and skip links whose available digests do not match.
When every available candidate archive hash conflicts with the locked metadata, Poetry should fail the install instead of selecting a mismatched distribution.

When the recorded hashes for an archive use only algorithms unavailable in the current Python runtime, Poetry should stop before installation and report a runtime failure rather than installing the package without validation.

task_7.title: Support custom wheel destination paths for packaged modules
task_7.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adds an optional `to` field to `tool.poetry.packages` so projects can relocate included packages or modules to a custom relative destination inside built wheel distributions. This expands packaging configuration flexibility while preserving existing source distribution behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `tool.poetry.packages` can declare a custom destination path so included packages or modules may be installed under a different relative location in generated wheel distributions.

expectation.grounded: Poetry should accept an optional string `to` key on entries in `tool.poetry.packages`. For package or module entries defined there, wheel builds should place the included files under the relative destination given by `to`, while source discovery should continue to honor `include` and optional `from`. Source distribution builds should continue to emit those files at their source-relative paths and not relocate them based on `to`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to configure where an included package or module ends up inside an installed wheel without changing where Poetry reads that content from on disk. The new destination setting should affect wheel output only and leave sdist layout unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Entries in `tool.poetry.packages` that do not specify `to` must retain their existing behavior. The optional `from` field must keep defining the source root for package discovery, while `to` only changes the relative destination path used for wheel contents. Existing `format` filtering semantics must continue to apply, and specifying `to` must not rename or relocate files in source distributions.
constraints.conceptual: This feature must be additive. Existing packaging configurations should keep working as before unless a destination path is explicitly configured, and changing wheel layout must not unexpectedly alter how source archives are structured.

behavior: An entry in `tool.poetry.packages` may include an optional string `to` field.
When building a wheel, Poetry relocates the selected package or module content under the relative destination path declared by `to`.
When both `from` and `to` are provided, Poetry reads content from the `from` location and writes it into the wheel under the `to` location.
When building an sdist, Poetry keeps the original source-relative paths even if `to` is configured.
If `to` is omitted, wheel and sdist packaging behavior remains unchanged from prior releases.
acceptance_criteria: When a package entry in `tool.poetry.packages` specifies `to`, building a wheel should place that package under the configured relative destination path.
When a single-module entry in `tool.poetry.packages` specifies `to`, building a wheel should place that module under the configured relative destination path.
When an entry specifies both `from` and `to`, Poetry should source files from the configured source location and emit them into the wheel at the configured destination location.
When the same project is built as an sdist, entries with `to` should still appear using their source-relative paths rather than the configured wheel destination path.
When no `to` field is configured, produced artifacts should preserve the packaging layout used before this update.

task_9.title: Support synchronized updates in Poetry
task_9.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adds a `--sync` option to `poetry update` so users can update dependencies and optionally synchronize the installed environment with the lock file for the selected dependency groups, aligning update behavior with install.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry update` provides an opt-in synchronization mode so users can update dependencies while also aligning the installed environment with the lock file for the selected dependency groups.

expectation.grounded: The `poetry update` command must accept a `--sync` option. When that option is present, the command should run its normal update flow and request environment synchronization against the locked packages for the selected dependency groups, matching the user-facing synchronization behavior already available on install. Existing update options such as dependency-group selection and `--dry-run` should continue to apply to the same invocation.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to ask an update to also clean up the environment so only packages that belong to the updated locked dependency set for the chosen groups remain installed.

constraints.grounded: Without `--sync`, `poetry update` must preserve its prior non-synchronizing behavior. Synchronization must remain optional, must respect the dependency-group scope chosen for the update command, and must not replace the normal update operation with a different command mode.
constraints.conceptual: Existing update workflows should behave the same unless synchronization is explicitly requested, and synchronization should only apply within the dependency scope the user selected.

behavior: `poetry update` exposes a new `--sync` flag.
Providing `--sync` causes the update operation to synchronize the environment with the locked packages for the selected dependency groups.
Running `poetry update` without `--sync` keeps the previous update behavior.
The synchronization option can be used together with existing update controls such as dependency-group selection and dry-run execution.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry update --sync`, the command should update dependencies and leave the environment synchronized to the resulting lock file for the selected dependency groups, removing packages that are outside that locked set.
When a user runs `poetry update` without `--sync`, the command should behave as before and should not require environment synchronization.
When a user combines `--sync` with dependency-group selection on `poetry update`, the synchronization should apply to that same selected group scope.
When a user combines `--sync` with `--dry-run`, the command should report the synchronized update operations without mutating the environment.

task_8.title: Allow disabling keyring integration via configuration
task_8.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adds a `keyring.enabled` setting so users can fully opt out of keyring probing, storage, and credential lookup. This prevents problematic keyring environments from interfering with authentication flows while preserving existing config- and environment-based credential behavior and warning when secrets are stored in plaintext.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can disable keyring completely through configuration so Poetry does not probe, read from, or write to keyring when that integration is causing problems, while still supporting repository credentials from environment variables or configuration files.

expectation.grounded: Expose `keyring.enabled` as a boolean configuration setting with a default of `true`, and gate all `PasswordManager` keyring usage on both that setting and `PoetryKeyring.is_available()`. When `keyring.enabled` is `false`, keyring availability checks and backend discovery must be bypassed, `set_pypi_token()` and `set_http_password()` must store credentials in the auth config source with the existing plaintext warning, and `get_pypi_token()`, `delete_pypi_token()`, `get_http_auth()`, `delete_http_password()`, and `get_credential()` must avoid keyring access. `PasswordManager.keyring` should raise `PoetryKeyringError` when keyring use is disabled or unavailable, and authenticator fallback to URL/netloc-based keyring credentials should only occur when keyring use is enabled.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to switch keyring off completely with `keyring.enabled`. After that, Poetry should behave as if keyring is unavailable: it should not inspect the system keyring, should not store or retrieve repository secrets there, should continue using environment/config-based credentials, should warn when it stores secrets in plaintext configuration, and should only report keyring access as unavailable if something explicitly asks for it.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing secure behavior when `keyring.enabled` is `true` and a usable backend exists: PyPI tokens and HTTP passwords should still use keyring storage, config or environment credentials should still take precedence before any keyring fallback, and backends identified as missing, fail, null, plaintext, or chainer without any valid chained backend must still be treated as unavailable.
constraints.conceptual: The new opt-out must not change normal credential handling for users with a working keyring, and it must not silently fall back to broken or insecure keyring backends. Disabling keyring must prevent side effects from keyring access without blocking non-keyring credential sources.

behavior: `keyring.enabled` is a new boolean configuration option, defaults to `true`, and is handled as a standard boolean config value.
Disabling `keyring.enabled` suppresses keyring availability checks and backend probing instead of merely ignoring keyring results later.
Keyring availability continues to reject unsuitable backends, including fail, null, plaintext, and chainer backends that do not contain any valid backend.
When keyring use is disabled or unavailable, direct access to `PasswordManager.keyring` raises `PoetryKeyringError`.
When keyring use is disabled, storing a PyPI token or HTTP basic password writes the secret to configuration storage and emits the existing plaintext-storage warning instead of using keyring.

When keyring use is disabled, token lookup, token deletion, HTTP auth lookup, and generic credential lookup do not call keyring; they only use environment/config-backed data and otherwise behave as if no password is available.
Repository authentication only falls back to URL/netloc-based keyring credentials when keyring use is enabled and the primary credential lookup did not already produce a password.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sets `keyring.enabled` to `false`, Poetry should accept the setting as valid configuration and stop treating keyring as an active credential source.
When `keyring.enabled` is `false`, operations that would normally inspect keyring availability or backends should complete without invoking keyring.
When `keyring.enabled` is `false` and a user stores a PyPI token or HTTP basic password, Poetry should persist that secret in configuration storage and warn that plaintext storage is being used.
When `keyring.enabled` is `false`, retrieving or deleting a PyPI token should use only non-keyring sources and should not attempt any keyring lookup.

When `keyring.enabled` is `false`, retrieving repository HTTP credentials should return credentials only if a complete username/password is available outside keyring; otherwise it should behave as though no password could be resolved.

When repository authentication resolves credentials from configured username data but no password is available, Poetry should only attempt URL/netloc-based keyring fallback if keyring remains enabled.
When `keyring.enabled` is `true` and a valid keyring backend exists, Poetry should continue using keyring-backed storage and lookup for repository credentials.

task_10.title: Support custom artifact output directories for build and publish
task_10.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adds a user-selectable destination for build artifacts and aligns publish-time builds with the publish command's chosen distribution directory, so packaging workflows are no longer tied to the default output folder.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that package build and publish workflows can target a user-selected artifact directory instead of always using the default distribution folder, while preserving existing build format validation and package-mode restrictions.

expectation.grounded: `poetry build` must accept a new `--output` (`-o`) option that selects the destination directory for generated sdist and wheel artifacts, defaulting to `dist` when omitted. Relative output paths must be resolved from the project root, while absolute paths must be used as provided. `poetry build` must continue to honor its `--format` selection rules and reject unsupported format values. In non-package mode, `poetry build` must fail instead of producing artifacts. `poetry publish` must support a `--dist-dir` workflow and, when it triggers a build, must direct `poetry build` to write artifacts into that same distribution directory.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to choose where build artifacts are created, and publish should use the same chosen artifact location whenever it builds packages on the user's behalf. The default behavior should remain unchanged for existing workflows, and invalid build modes or unsupported formats should still be rejected.

constraints.grounded: Omitting `--output` must continue to place artifacts in the project's default `dist` directory. Changing the output directory must not change which package formats are built; it only changes where the resulting archives are written. Publish-triggered builds must not fall back to the default directory when a non-default `--dist-dir` is selected. Non-package-mode projects must remain ineligible for building.
constraints.conceptual: Existing users who do not opt into a custom artifact directory should see no change in where packages are created. Choosing a different destination should only redirect artifact placement, not alter package contents, format selection, or whether the project is buildable. Build and publish should stay consistent about where artifacts live.

behavior: `poetry build` accepts a new `--output` (`-o`) option for selecting the artifact destination directory.
When no output directory is supplied, `poetry build` continues to write artifacts to the default `dist` directory for the project.
When the output directory is relative, Poetry resolves it relative to the project root; when it is absolute, Poetry writes artifacts directly there.
`poetry build` still limits builds to supported format selections and rejects unsupported format values.
`poetry build` fails in non-package mode instead of attempting to create build artifacts.
When `poetry publish` performs a build with a selected `--dist-dir`, it forwards that directory to the build step so the produced artifacts are stored where publish expects them.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry build` without `--output`, the requested archives should be created in the project's default `dist` directory.
When a user runs `poetry build --output <relative-directory>`, the requested archives should be created under that directory relative to the project root.
When a user runs `poetry build --output <absolute-directory>`, the requested archives should be created in that absolute directory.
When a user supplies an unsupported `--format` value to `poetry build`, the command should fail instead of silently building another format.
When `poetry build` is run for a project in non-package mode, it should refuse to build and report failure.

When a user runs `poetry publish` with a non-default `--dist-dir` and publish triggers a build, the build artifacts should be generated in that same distribution directory and then used for publishing.

task_11.title: Support configurable artifact directories in poetry publish
task_11.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adds a `--dist-dir` option to `poetry publish` so users can publish distributions from a chosen artifact directory instead of only the default `dist` folder. The publish flow must use that directory consistently for artifact discovery and build-then-publish workflows, and it must fail early when publishing is attempted in non-package mode.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry publish` can publish distributions from a user-specified artifact directory, that `--build` writes artifacts to and publishes from that same directory, and that publishing is rejected when the project is not operating in package mode.

expectation.grounded: The `poetry publish` command must accept `--dist-dir <path>` with `dist` as the default. Artifact discovery used by publishing, including the source distribution lookup needed for package registration, must read from the configured distribution directory instead of always using the default location. Relative `--dist-dir` values must be resolved from the project directory, while absolute paths must be honored directly. When `poetry publish --build` is used, the build step must target the same directory via the build command's output option before publish scans for files. If package mode is disabled, `poetry publish` must stop immediately, report that publishing is not possible in non-package mode, and return a non-zero exit status.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to keep build artifacts outside the default folder and still publish them with `poetry publish`. The publish flow should treat the chosen artifact directory as the single source of truth for both existing artifacts and artifacts created during a build-then-publish run. Projects that are not publishable packages should fail fast instead of attempting any publishing work.

constraints.grounded: Omitting `--dist-dir` must preserve the existing default behavior of using the project's `dist` directory. Supplying a custom directory must only change where publish looks for and produces artifacts; it must not change artifact name/version matching, upload handling, or dry-run behavior. Relative paths must remain project-root-relative rather than shell-working-directory-relative.
constraints.conceptual: Existing users should see no behavior change unless they opt into a custom artifact directory. Custom directory support should be additive and consistent, without changing what counts as a publishable artifact or how publish behaves apart from where artifacts are read from and written to.

behavior: `poetry publish` accepts a new `--dist-dir` option and defaults it to `dist` when unspecified.
Publishing resolves relative distribution directories from the project root and uses absolute distribution directories as provided.
The publish command reads candidate distribution files from the configured artifact directory rather than only from the default `dist` folder.
Source distribution lookup used during package registration also uses the configured artifact directory.
When `--build` is combined with `--dist-dir`, publish invokes the build step so newly built artifacts are emitted into the same configured directory before upload begins.
If the project is in non-package mode, `poetry publish` exits with a failure status before any build or upload work is attempted.
acceptance_criteria: When a package's built distributions exist in a non-default relative directory and the user runs `poetry publish --dist-dir <relative-path>`, the command should publish the artifacts from that directory.
When the user runs `poetry publish --dist-dir <absolute-path>`, the command should use that absolute directory for artifact discovery and publishing.
When the user omits `--dist-dir`, `poetry publish` should behave as before and use the default project `dist` directory.
When the user runs `poetry publish --build --dist-dir <path>`, the build output and the subsequent publish step should both target the same configured directory.

When the project is configured in non-package mode and the user runs `poetry publish`, the command should fail immediately with a non-zero exit status and a user-visible indication that publishing is unavailable in non-package mode.

task_12.title: Require explicit PyPI with primary sources
task_12.description: Poetry 1.8.0 no longer keeps the implicit PyPI source enabled when a project configures any primary package source, so projects that still need PyPI alongside custom primary sources must declare it explicitly. When no default or primary source is configured, Poetry still adds PyPI automatically, but it now treats that fallback source as primary rather than default.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects upgrading to Poetry 1.8.0 do not rely on PyPI remaining implicitly available once any primary package source is configured, and that automatic PyPI fallback uses the new primary-source semantics.

expectation.grounded: If `PyPI` is not configured explicitly, Poetry must omit the implicit `PyPI` repository whenever the configured source pool already contains a default repository or any primary repository. If no default or primary repository exists, Poetry must continue auto-adding `PyPI`, but that auto-added repository should have `Priority.PRIMARY` rather than `Priority.DEFAULT`. Projects that need both custom primary sources and `PyPI` must declare `PyPI` explicitly.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading to 1.8.0 should make repository selection explicit: once a project chooses a primary source, Poetry should only use the sources the project names unless PyPI is also named. Projects with no primary or default source should still get PyPI automatically, and that automatic PyPI source should behave like a normal primary source.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove automatic PyPI availability for projects that have no configured default or primary repository and have not explicitly configured `PyPI`. Do not change the behavior of explicitly configured `PyPI`; only the implicit fallback behavior should change. Source selection should reflect the new runtime behavior directly rather than a warning-only transition.
constraints.conceptual: Keep PyPI as the default fallback only for projects that have not selected another primary or default source. Do not silently continue querying PyPI for projects that have already opted into explicit primary sources.

behavior: When at least one primary repository is configured and `PyPI` is not explicitly configured, `PyPI` is no longer added implicitly to the active repository set.
The prior transitional warning about future implicit PyPI deactivation is replaced by immediate runtime deactivation.
When no default or primary repository is configured and `PyPI` is not explicitly configured, Poetry still auto-registers `PyPI`.
An auto-registered `PyPI` repository now uses primary priority instead of default priority.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project with a custom primary source and no explicit PyPI source, when Poetry loads the configured repositories, then PyPI should not be present or queried.
Given a project with multiple custom primary sources and no explicit PyPI source, when Poetry loads the configured repositories, then only the declared sources should participate.
Given a project with no configured default or primary source and no explicit PyPI source, when Poetry loads the configured repositories, then PyPI should still be available automatically.

Given a project that relies on automatically added PyPI because no primary or default source is configured, when Poetry loads that source in 1.8.0, then it should behave as a primary source rather than a special default source.
Given a project that needs both custom primary sources and PyPI, when it upgrades to 1.8.0, then PyPI should participate only if it is declared explicitly.

task_14.title: Fail Fast on Inconsistent Poetry Lockfiles
task_14.description: Poetry 1.8.0 stops treating an inconsistent lockfile as a warning-only condition. When `poetry.lock` is no longer in sync with `pyproject.toml`, installation now fails immediately instead of continuing with stale locked dependency data that can lead to misleading downstream version errors.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency installation aborts when `poetry.lock` is inconsistent with `pyproject.toml`, instead of warning and continuing with stale lock data that can produce confusing dependency resolution failures.

expectation.grounded: When `Installer.run()` takes the lockfile-based installation path and `Locker.is_fresh()` reports false, the operation should raise `ValueError` for the inconsistent `poetry.lock` and `pyproject.toml` state rather than emitting a warning and proceeding with locked dependency data. When the lockfile is fresh, the existing lock-based installation flow should continue unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: If the project definition has diverged from the lockfile, Poetry should fail fast with a clear error that tells the user the lockfile must be refreshed, rather than attempting to install from outdated pins.

constraints.grounded: Do not continue installation after the stale-lockfile check fails, and do not downgrade that condition back to warning-only output. Do not change behavior for runs where the lockfile remains fresh and consistent with the project definition.
constraints.conceptual: Reject only the inconsistent lockfile state, preserve normal behavior for valid lockfiles, and surface the problem at the point it is detected instead of allowing later, less accurate dependency errors to appear first.

behavior: A lockfile inconsistency between `pyproject.toml` and `poetry.lock` is treated as an error condition during installation.
The installer raises `ValueError` when the lockfile freshness check fails.
Installation does not proceed to use stale lockfile dependency data once the inconsistency is detected.
Projects with a fresh, consistent lockfile continue through the normal lock-based installation path.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project whose `poetry.lock` is no longer fresh relative to `pyproject.toml`, when a dependency operation invokes the installer, it should terminate with `ValueError` instead of only printing a warning.
When the inconsistent lockfile condition is detected, the installer should stop before continuing with lockfile-derived dependency installation.
When the lockfile is consistent with the project definition, lockfile-based installation should still proceed normally.

When users encounter this stale lockfile condition, the failure should clearly indicate that the lockfile needs to be regenerated rather than leaving the first visible problem as a downstream missing-version style error.

task_13.title: Deprecate default source priority and require explicit PyPI with primary sources
task_13.description: Poetry 1.8.0 finalizes its source-priority transition. Configurations that rely on the deprecated `default` source priority now emit warnings, and projects with a custom primary package source no longer keep an implicit PyPI source unless PyPI is declared explicitly. This changes observable dependency source selection during the upgrade.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Poetry 1.8.0 no longer relies on the deprecated `default` source priority or on implicit PyPI remaining active when a custom primary source is configured.

expectation.grounded: Poetry should continue accepting source definitions that use `priority = "default"` in `pyproject.toml` and through `poetry source add --priority=default`, but it should emit a deprecation warning and treat the supported replacement as using `priority = "primary"` with source order determining precedence. When PyPI is not configured explicitly, Poetry should automatically disable the implicit PyPI repository as soon as any custom primary source exists; if no default or primary source exists, Poetry should still add the implicit PyPI repository and expose it as a primary source.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, source configuration should express preferred indexes with ordered primary sources instead of a special default priority. Users must explicitly add PyPI if they want it searched alongside a custom primary index, while existing deprecated configurations should still work with warnings rather than immediate failure.

constraints.grounded: The upgrade should preserve backward compatibility for deprecated `default` and `secondary` priorities by warning instead of rejecting them. Explicit PyPI configuration must continue to override implicit PyPI behavior, and projects without any primary or default source must not lose PyPI access.
constraints.conceptual: The change should steer users toward the new source model without silently removing plain PyPI access from configurations that still depend on it, and it should not turn these deprecations into hard failures in this release.

behavior: Using a source with `priority = "default"` now triggers a deprecation warning during Poetry configuration loading.
Running `poetry source add` with `--priority=default` still adds the source but warns that `default` is deprecated.
Running `poetry source add` with `--priority=secondary` still warns about deprecation, and its recommendation set no longer includes `default` as a preferred alternative.
If a project defines at least one custom primary source and does not explicitly configure PyPI, Poetry no longer adds the implicit PyPI repository.
If a project does not define a default or primary source and does not explicitly configure PyPI, Poetry still adds PyPI implicitly and treats it as a primary source.
acceptance_criteria: When a project contains a source declared with `priority = "default"`, Poetry should continue loading the project and emit a deprecation warning for that source.
When `poetry source add --priority=default <name> <url>` is used, Poetry should add the source and emit a deprecation warning instead of failing.
When a project has a custom primary source and does not declare PyPI explicitly, Poetry should resolve packages without an implicit PyPI source being active.
When a project has no custom default or primary source and does not declare PyPI explicitly, Poetry should still make PyPI available as a primary source.
When `poetry source add --priority=secondary` is used, Poetry should warn about deprecation and recommend only non-deprecated priorities.

task_15.title: Deprecate legacy installer opt-out
task_15.description: Poetry 1.8.0 deprecates configuring `installer.modern-installation` as `false`. Existing installs may still run through the legacy installer path, but users who rely on that setting must now receive a visible deprecation notice that the pip-based installer is temporary and planned for removal.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users who still configure `installer.modern-installation` as `false` are explicitly warned that this legacy installer mode is deprecated and will be removed in a future release, while current installation behavior continues to work for now.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry resolves the `installer.modern-installation` configuration value to `false`, it should emit a user-visible deprecation warning during installation setup. The warning should state that `installer.modern-installation=false` is deprecated, that the pip-based installer will be removed in a future release, and should direct users to the published deprecation context. If the setting is unset or `true`, no deprecation warning should be emitted for this feature.
expectation.conceptual: Users who opt out of the modern installer should be clearly informed at runtime that they are on a deprecated path and need to migrate away from it, without breaking their current install flow immediately.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove support for `installer.modern-installation=false` in this release. Preserve the existing default behavior when the setting is absent by continuing to treat modern installation as enabled. The only new observable effect for the deprecated configuration is warning output; execution should continue instead of failing solely because the setting is `false`.
constraints.conceptual: Maintain backward compatibility for existing users in this version. Only users who rely on the deprecated legacy mode should see the new notice, and the notice must not turn the configuration into an immediate error.

behavior: Poetry continues to read `installer.modern-installation` with modern installation enabled by default when the setting is not provided.
If `installer.modern-installation` is set to `false`, Poetry emits a visible deprecation warning during installer initialization.
The warning communicates both that the `false` setting is deprecated and that the legacy pip-based installer is scheduled for future removal.
Using the deprecated setting remains operational in 1.8.0; the change is advisory rather than an immediate removal or failure.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs an installation flow with `installer.modern-installation=false`, the command should display a deprecation warning before continuing.
When a user runs an installation flow with `installer.modern-installation` unset or set to `true`, no deprecation warning related to this setting should be shown.
When the deprecated setting is used, the warning should make clear that the legacy pip-based installer is temporary and will be removed in a future release.
Using `installer.modern-installation=false` in 1.8.0 should not by itself abort or reject the installation flow.

task_17.title: Require requests-toolbelt 1.x for urllib3 compatibility
task_17.description: Version 1.8.0 raises the minimum supported requests-toolbelt version to 1.0.0 or newer so dependency resolution produces a combination that remains compatible with urllib3-backed HTTP functionality.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 1.8.0 requires a requests-toolbelt release that is compatible with urllib3, so users do not end up with unsupported 0.x dependency combinations that can break HTTP-related behavior.

expectation.grounded: The 1.8.0 release should require requests-toolbelt>=1. Dependency resolution for the library should no longer allow requests-toolbelt 0.x, and runtime behavior that depends on the requests/urllib3 stack should execute against a supported requests-toolbelt major version.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, users should automatically get a modern requests-toolbelt version that works with the library's HTTP stack, avoiding compatibility failures caused by outdated transitive dependencies.

constraints.grounded: Do not accept requests-toolbelt versions below 1.0.0 in 1.8.0. Keep the change scoped to dependency compatibility with urllib3 rather than altering unrelated public behavior or workflows.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should tighten dependency compatibility without changing normal user workflows beyond preventing unsupported dependency combinations.

behavior: Installing or resolving version 1.8.0 requires requests-toolbelt version 1.0.0 or newer.
Environments that pin or resolve requests-toolbelt 0.x are no longer valid for version 1.8.0 and should surface a dependency incompatibility instead of being silently accepted.
HTTP-related library behavior that relies on the requests and urllib3 stack is expected to run with a requests-toolbelt version compatible with current urllib3 support.
acceptance_criteria: When a user installs or upgrades to version 1.8.0 in a clean environment, the resolved dependency set should include requests-toolbelt>=1.
When a user attempts to use version 1.8.0 with requests-toolbelt below 1.0.0, the unsupported dependency combination should be rejected during dependency resolution or installation.
When the upgraded library performs HTTP-dependent operations, it should not rely on an older requests-toolbelt release that is incompatible with urllib3.

task_16.title: Remove legacy pip<19 installation compatibility
task_16.description: Poetry 1.8.0 drops support for environments that rely on pip older than 19. Installation logic no longer selects a legacy compatibility path based on pip version, and instead assumes a modern pip/build-system-capable environment by default, while still preserving the special fallback for packages that explicitly declare a build script.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Poetry 1.8.0 no longer supports `pip` versions below 19, and that installation behavior consistently uses the modern build-system-aware flow for Poetry-managed packages unless a package explicitly requires the legacy build-script fallback.

expectation.grounded: Poetry should stop detecting or branching on `pip<19` during package installation. For Poetry-managed packages, editable installs without a declared `build_script` should continue to behave as editable installs, packages with a declared `build_script` should continue to use the legacy source-distribution-based fallback, and packages without a `build_script` should otherwise be installed through the standard modern pip/build-system flow.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should require a modern pip and remove special handling for very old pip releases. Normal packages should install through the standard modern workflow, editable installs should keep working, and only packages that explicitly depend on a legacy build script should still use the older fallback behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not preserve a dedicated compatibility path that exists only for `pip<19`. Do not change the existing editable-install behavior for Poetry-managed packages that have no `build_script`. Do not remove the legacy fallback for packages that explicitly declare `build_script`.
constraints.conceptual: Keep behavior stable for supported modern environments, preserve compatibility for packages that explicitly need legacy script-based builds, and avoid retaining support guarantees for outdated pip versions.

behavior: Installation decisions no longer depend on the detected pip version.
The legacy fallback path is no longer triggered solely because the environment is using `pip` older than 19.
Editable installation of a Poetry-managed package without a declared `build_script` remains supported.
A Poetry-managed package that declares `build_script` continues to use the legacy source-distribution-based installation path.
A Poetry-managed package without `build_script` is now always treated as requiring the modern pip/build-system-aware installation flow.
acceptance_criteria: When a user upgrades to Poetry 1.8.0, environments that depend on `pip` older than 19 should no longer be considered supported.
When installing a Poetry-managed package that does not declare `build_script`, Poetry should not switch to a legacy install path solely because of pip version.
When installing a Poetry-managed package with `develop` enabled and no declared `build_script`, Poetry should continue to perform an editable install.
When installing a Poetry-managed package that declares `build_script`, Poetry should continue to use the legacy fallback installation behavior.

task_19.title: Require xattr 1.x on macOS
task_19.description: Version 1.8.0 updates the macOS xattr dependency so the project accepts and requires the 1.x line, fixing installation and build failures caused by the missing xattr/lib_build.h file in the older dependency path.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that macOS installations and upgrades use a supported `xattr` 1.x dependency so users do not hit failures caused by the missing `xattr/lib_build.h` file.

expectation.grounded: On macOS, dependency resolution for `xattr` should allow and require the 1.x major version. Installing or upgrading the package in macOS environments should no longer fail because of the missing `xattr/lib_build.h` issue tied to the older `xattr` dependency path.
expectation.conceptual: macOS users should automatically receive a compatible `xattr` version during installation or upgrade, and the update should remove the dependency-related failure caused by incomplete upstream packaging.

constraints.grounded: The change is scoped to macOS handling of the `xattr` dependency. macOS resolution should not continue accepting older incompatible `xattr` major versions, and non-macOS environments should not gain a new `xattr` requirement from this change.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the fix limited to platform-specific dependency compatibility: macOS should consistently use the supported dependency line, while other platforms continue behaving as before.

behavior: On macOS, the package now accepts `xattr` 1.x as the supported dependency line.
On macOS, the package requires `xattr` 1.x rather than relying on older `xattr` versions.
Installing or upgrading on macOS no longer fails due to the missing `xattr/lib_build.h` issue that prompted the dependency bump.
acceptance_criteria: When a user installs or upgrades the package on macOS, dependency resolution should select a compatible `xattr` 1.x release.
When the package is installed on macOS, it should not fail because the resolved `xattr` package is missing `xattr/lib_build.h`.
When the package is installed on non-macOS platforms, this change should not introduce a new `xattr` dependency requirement.

task_20.title: Improve interactive virtualenv activation for fish shells
task_20.description: Poetry 1.8.0 changes `poetry shell` so `fish` sessions start with the virtual environment already activated instead of visibly replaying the activation command in the terminal. The shell activation flow also preserves startup-based activation for shells that already support it and tightens command quoting for `zsh` activation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry shell` opens a clean, already-activated interactive shell for `fish` users and preserves reliable activation behavior across other supported shells.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry shell` detects `fish`, it should launch the interactive shell with the virtualenv activation command supplied as part of shell startup so the prompt appears already activated. `nu` should continue to activate during shell invocation rather than by sending a follow-up command, and `zsh` activation through bash emulation should preserve safe quoting of the activation path.
expectation.conceptual: Starting a Poetry-managed shell should immediately place the user in an activated environment without showing a typed activation command in the session, while keeping shell activation dependable across supported shell types.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress activation behavior for existing supported shells such as `nu`, `xonsh`, `zsh`, or other interactive shells. Shells that activate at startup must not also receive a duplicate post-launch activation command, and shell-specific activation commands must remain safely quoted when environment paths contain characters that require escaping.
constraints.conceptual: Keep current shell support intact, avoid duplicate activation side effects, and ensure activation remains safe and reliable even when environment paths are not simple.

behavior: `poetry shell` on `fish` should start an interactive `fish` session with virtualenv activation applied during shell startup.
Because `fish` activation happens at startup, the session should no longer display the activation command as if it were manually entered before the first prompt.
`nu` should continue using startup-time activation instead of receiving a post-launch activation command.
`zsh` activation should continue to work through bash emulation while preserving correct quoting of the activation command and target path.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry shell` and the detected shell is `fish`, the first interactive prompt should already reflect an active Poetry virtual environment.
When `poetry shell` starts a `fish` session, it should not print or replay a standalone activation command into the terminal before the prompt appears.
When the detected shell is `nu`, environment activation should still occur as part of shell startup rather than as an injected command after launch.
When `poetry shell` activates an environment through `zsh`, activation should remain successful for environment paths that require shell-safe quoting.

task_18.title: Support platformdirs 4.x for Poetry
task_18.description: Poetry 1.8.0 broadens its own dependency compatibility so it can be installed with platformdirs 4.x as well as 3.x. This removes avoidable version conflicts in user environments while keeping Poetry behavior unchanged because the upstream site_cache_dir change in platformdirs 4.x is not part of the surface Poetry uses.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry can be installed and used when its environment resolves platformdirs 4.x, while preserving compatibility with supported 3.x releases and avoiding user-visible regressions in Poetry behavior.

expectation.grounded: Poetry's declared dependency on platformdirs should accept versions >=3.0.0 and <5 instead of only the 3.x line. A Poetry installation resolved with platformdirs 4.x should install and run without dependency-range failures, and no behavior change is required around platformdirs.site_cache_dir because Poetry does not use the upstream API surface whose behavior changed in 4.x.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to Poetry 1.8.0 should be able to install and use it in environments that provide platformdirs 4.x, with the same observable Poetry behavior as before.

constraints.grounded: Retain compatibility with platformdirs 3.x, do not widen support beyond major version 4, and do not introduce behavior that depends on platformdirs.site_cache_dir or its changed location in platformdirs 4.x.
constraints.conceptual: Expand supported dependency versions without changing normal Poetry behavior or implying compatibility with unsupported future major versions.

behavior: Poetry's dependency metadata accepts platformdirs 4.x as a valid version for Poetry itself.
Poetry continues to accept platformdirs 3.x.
Platformdirs 5.x and newer remain outside the supported version range.
Using platformdirs 4.x should not create a user-visible Poetry behavior change solely from the upstream site_cache_dir relocation.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry 1.8.0 is installed in an environment where dependency resolution selects platformdirs 4.x, the installation should succeed without a version-constraint conflict.
When Poetry 1.8.0 is installed with platformdirs 3.x, it should remain supported and behave as before.
When an unsupported platformdirs major version such as 5.x is selected for Poetry itself, it should still be treated as out of range.
When users run Poetry with platformdirs 4.x installed, they should not observe a behavior change attributable only to the upstream site_cache_dir relocation.

task_21.title: Rename `poetry env info` parent interpreter output from System to Base
task_21.description: Poetry 1.8.0 updates the human-readable output of `poetry env info` so the interpreter that underlies the active virtual environment is described as the base Python rather than the system Python. This keeps the command accurate when the selected base interpreter is not the operating system's default Python.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry env info` describes the interpreter underlying the active virtual environment as `Base` instead of `System`, so the output does not imply that this interpreter is always the operating system's system Python.

expectation.grounded: The human-readable output of `poetry env info` should still include virtual environment details plus a second section for the parent interpreter, but that second section should be labeled `Base`. The `Base` section should continue to expose the observable parent-interpreter fields shown by the command: platform, OS, Python version, installation path, and executable.
expectation.conceptual: Users inspecting an environment should see the underlying interpreter described as the base Python for that environment, while the same interpreter metadata remains available.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove or rename the existing virtual environment section, and do not change the meaning of the reported parent-interpreter metadata beyond replacing the `System` terminology with `Base`. The command should continue reporting the same underlying interpreter values for the active environment.
constraints.conceptual: This should be a terminology correction for the secondary interpreter section only; the rest of the environment report and the interpreter facts it shows should stay the same.

behavior: `poetry env info` labels the section for the environment's parent interpreter as `Base` instead of `System`.
The renamed section continues to describe the interpreter from which the active environment derives, even when that interpreter is not the operating system's default Python.
The `Base` section continues to present platform, OS, Python version, installation path, and executable details for that interpreter.
acceptance_criteria: When running `poetry env info`, the output should show the secondary interpreter section under the heading `Base`.
When the active environment is based on a Python interpreter that is not the machine's system Python, the command should still describe it as the base interpreter rather than the system interpreter.
When `poetry env info` displays base interpreter details, it should continue to include platform, OS, Python version, installation path, and executable information.

task_22.title: Preserve declared package name in `poetry version` output
task_22.description: The 1.8.0 update changes the default display output of `poetry version` so it shows the package name as declared for users, instead of Poetry's normalized internal name. This improves CLI and automation readability while keeping version-only output behavior unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry version` displays the project name in its user-facing form when reporting the current package version, so command-line users and automation receive the declared package name instead of a normalized variant.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry version` is used to show the current version in its default output mode, it should print `self.poetry.package.pretty_name` together with `self.poetry.package.pretty_version`, rather than using the normalized `self.poetry.package.name`. The `--short` mode should continue to emit only the version string.
expectation.conceptual: The default `poetry version` command output should show the package name exactly as users define it in project metadata, alongside the current version. Short output should remain a version-only view.

constraints.grounded: Only the package-name portion of the default display output should change. The reported version value should remain the package's current pretty version, and `poetry version --short` must keep omitting the package name entirely.
constraints.conceptual: This update should adjust name presentation without changing how the version itself is reported or altering the compact version-only mode.

behavior: Running `poetry version` without requesting short output now shows the package's declared display name instead of its normalized internal name.
If the declared package name preserves formatting that differs from normalization, such as underscores, the displayed name should preserve that formatting in the command output.
The version shown by `poetry version` remains the same current package version as before; only the displayed package name source changes.
Running `poetry version --short` continues to return only the current version and does not include the package name.
acceptance_criteria: When a project's declared package name differs from its normalized form, running `poetry version` should display the declared name followed by the current version.

When a project's declared package name already matches its normalized form, running `poetry version` should continue to produce the same visible name-and-version shape apart from the updated name source.
When `poetry version --short` is run, it should output only the current version and should not include the package name.
When `poetry version` is used for display, the version portion of the output should remain the current package version and should not change as part of this update.

task_23.title: Improve invalid Poetry script entry errors
task_23.description: Poetry 1.8.0 improves how editable builds handle malformed `tool.poetry.scripts` definitions. Instead of surfacing a generic parsing failure, it now raises targeted validation errors that identify the bad script entry, explain the required `module:function` shape, distinguish between missing and extra colon separators, and preserve parsing of the callable target separately from any extras suffix.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that malformed `tool.poetry.scripts` entries fail with actionable validation errors during editable build or install, so users can identify whether a console script is missing its callable separator or contains too many separators.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry processes `tool.poetry.scripts` into `console_scripts` for an editable build, each entry must be interpretable as `name = module(.submodule):function`, with any optional extras suffix excluded from module and callable parsing. If parsing the `module:function` portion fails, Poetry should raise `ValueError` that identifies the bad script by name, shows the configured value, states that a function within a module is required, and differentiates between entries with no `:` and entries with more than one `:`. For missing `:`, the error should also provide corrective guidance that the script should point to a callable such as `main` rather than bare module-level code.
expectation.conceptual: Editable installs should validate script definitions in `tool.poetry.scripts` and report configuration mistakes clearly. A script entry should reference a callable inside a module. If the callable separator is missing, users should be told that the script points to a module instead of a function and be given actionable guidance. If multiple separators are present, users should be told that the format is invalid because the script target is ambiguous.

constraints.grounded: Valid `tool.poetry.scripts` entries that resolve to a single `module:function` target must continue to build normally. Error handling must only change the failure mode for malformed script entries, keep the reported script value user-visible, and continue deriving the wrapper target from the callable holder portion before the first `.` in the callable path.
