constraints.conceptual: Correctly defined scripts should behave as before. The change should only make invalid script configuration failures clearer, without changing successful script generation or broadening the accepted format beyond a single callable target inside a module.

behavior: During editable build or install, Poetry validates each `console_scripts` entry generated from `tool.poetry.scripts` before creating the script wrapper.
Poetry parses the script target from the `module:function` portion of the configured value and ignores any optional extras suffix for that validation step.

If a script entry has no `:` separator, Poetry raises `ValueError` that names the script, includes the configured value, explains that a function target is required, and provides guidance to point the script at a callable such as `main`.

If a script entry contains more than one `:` separator, Poetry raises `ValueError` that names the script, includes the configured value, explains that the format is invalid, and indicates that too many separators were supplied.
Malformed script entries no longer surface a low-context internal parsing failure.
acceptance_criteria: When an editable build processes a `tool.poetry.scripts` entry with exactly one `module:function` target, it should continue generating the console script successfully.

When an editable build processes a `tool.poetry.scripts` entry that names only a module and no callable, it should fail with `ValueError` that identifies the script entry and clearly explains that a callable target is required.

When an editable build processes a `tool.poetry.scripts` entry with more than one `:` separator, it should fail with `ValueError` that identifies the script entry and clearly explains that the definition contains too many separators.
When an invalid `tool.poetry.scripts` entry is reported, the error should expose the user-configured value so the misconfiguration can be corrected directly.
When a script target includes an extras suffix, validation should be based on the underlying `module:function` target rather than treating the extras marker as part of the callable path.

task_24.title: Preserve extras in verbose dependency resolution output
task_24.description: Dependency resolution output now keeps the requested extras attached to dependency names in verbose solver explanations, while reusing the same candidate lookup for the base package so the reported dependency relationships match the user's declared requirement.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that verbose dependency-resolution output preserves extras on declared dependencies, so commands such as `poetry lock -vv` identify `foo[bar]` as an extra-enabled requirement instead of collapsing it to the base package name.

expectation.grounded: During solver explanations and incompatibility rendering, dependencies with extras should be displayed using their complete pretty name, including extras, while still showing the applicable version constraint. Dependency candidate caching should treat dependencies that differ only by extras as the same underlying package lookup by base package and source identity, but when cached results are surfaced for an extra-enabled dependency, the dependency context returned to the solver must retain the requested extras and any explicit source information already attached to the cached dependency.
expectation.conceptual: When verbose dependency resolution explains why one package depends on another, the output should reflect the exact dependency the user asked for, including extras. Internally equivalent lookups for the same package should not lose that extra-qualified identity in the user-visible explanation.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing rendering path for dependencies that already carry an explicit source representation; those should continue to use their source-aware string form. Dependencies without extras should continue to render with the existing package-name and constraint format, and this change should not alter which package versions are considered candidates for resolution.
constraints.conceptual: Improve identification of extra-enabled dependencies without changing dependency-selection outcomes or regressing the existing output format for plain dependencies and direct-source dependencies.

behavior: Verbose incompatibility and dependency-cause output now shows the depender's extras when the dependency was declared with extras.
Dependencies that differ only by requested extras share the same cached candidate package search instead of being treated as separate package-name lookups.
When cached candidates are reused for an extra-enabled dependency, the solver-visible dependency context keeps the requested extras so later output still reflects the original requirement shape.
Dependencies with explicit source information continue to render using their source-qualified dependency representation.
acceptance_criteria: When verbose dependency resolution is run for a dependency declared with extras, the explanatory output should identify that dependency with its extras included.
When the same package is encountered both with and without extras during a resolution pass, the extra-enabled occurrence should still be reported in its extra-enabled form in verbose solver output.
When a dependency has no extras, verbose dependency-cause output should remain in the existing plain name-and-constraint style.
When a dependency comes from an explicit source such as a URL or similar source-qualified reference, verbose output should continue to present the source-qualified dependency form.

task_27.title: Prevent CLI output encoding failures in non-UTF-8 terminals
task_27.description: Poetry 1.8.0 removes non-ASCII bullet markers from user-visible command output and replaces them with ASCII hyphens so package operation and plugin listing commands continue to work in terminals that are not configured for UTF-8.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry commands which print package-operation or plugin-list entries do not fail in terminals using a non-UTF-8 encoding, while preserving the same visible progress, status, and package information.

expectation.grounded: Poetry command output for package operations and list entries should use ASCII hyphen prefixes instead of Unicode bullet characters. This applies to operation progress and result lines emitted during install, update, downgrade, remove, download, prepare, build, clone, skipped, failed, and cancelled states, as well as list-style output from commands such as `poetry add` and `poetry self show plugins`. Commands should still emit the same package names, versions, reasons, and status labels without raising terminal encoding errors solely because of these prefixes.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry prints list-like status lines, it should use terminal-safe text so the command output remains readable and the command completes normally even on non-UTF-8 terminals. Users should see the same operational information as before, with only the list marker style changing from a special symbol to a plain ASCII character.

constraints.grounded: Do not change which operations are reported, when statuses are shown, or the accompanying package/version/status information. ANSI styling and normal command flow should continue to work; only the marker character used at the start of these lines should become ASCII-safe.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the behavior and meaning of command output the same apart from using a more compatible list marker. The fix should improve terminal compatibility without altering the underlying package actions or reducing the detail shown to users.

behavior: Package operation lines printed during dependency installation workflows use a hyphen prefix instead of a Unicode bullet.
The same ASCII-safe prefix is used for pending, installing, downloading, preparing, building, cloning, removing, completed, skipped, failed, and cancelled operation messages.
List-style output shown when `poetry add` reports already-present packages uses a hyphen prefix instead of a Unicode bullet.
List-style output shown by `poetry self show plugins` uses a hyphen prefix instead of a Unicode bullet.

Commands that previously risked failing when writing Unicode bullet characters to a non-UTF-8 terminal should now complete without that encoding failure, assuming no other unrelated output issue occurs.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry runs in a terminal configured with a non-UTF-8 encoding and prints package operation progress, it should complete without failing solely because it tried to emit a list marker character.

When a command reports package operations such as install, update, downgrade, remove, skip, failure, or cancellation, the line should begin with an ASCII hyphen and still show the same operation details and statuses.
When `poetry add` reports dependencies that are already present, it should render each listed package with an ASCII hyphen prefix and continue normally.
When `poetry self show plugins` lists installed plugins, it should render each entry with an ASCII hyphen prefix and continue normally.
When ANSI-colored output is enabled, the status lines should remain styled and readable while using the ASCII-safe marker.

task_25.title: Fail fast on outdated lockfiles with clearer guidance
task_25.description: Poetry 1.8.0 tightens outdated lockfile handling by describing stale lock state more clearly and preventing install workflows from proceeding when `poetry.lock` no longer matches `pyproject.toml`. This avoids continuing with potentially incorrect dependency resolution and gives users a clearer recovery path.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that a significantly outdated `poetry.lock` is treated as an actionable error, not a soft warning, and that lockfile-related commands consistently explain that the lock file must be regenerated after meaningful `pyproject.toml` changes.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry.lock` exists but is outdated relative to `pyproject.toml`, `poetry check --lock` and the deprecated `poetry lock --check` should surface a consistent error indicating that the project definition changed since the lock file was last generated and direct the user to refresh it with `poetry lock [--no-update]`. Installation paths that rely on the current lock file should no longer continue after only warning; they should fail by raising `ValueError` when the lock is not fresh.
expectation.conceptual: If the project metadata has changed enough that the lockfile is no longer current, Poetry should clearly tell users that the lockfile is outdated and stop any workflow that depends on that stale lockfile until it is regenerated.

constraints.grounded: The stale-lock condition should be handled consistently across lock-checking commands and install-time lock reuse. Fresh lockfiles should continue to allow normal execution, and existing handling for a missing `poetry.lock` should remain intact. The change should not silently permit installation against a known stale lockfile.
constraints.conceptual: Only the outdated-lockfile scenario should become stricter. Valid lockfiles should continue to work normally, and users should not be allowed to proceed on a dependency state that Poetry already knows is out of sync.

behavior: `poetry check --lock` reports an outdated lockfile as an error framed around `pyproject.toml` having changed since `poetry.lock` was generated, with guidance to regenerate the lock file.
The deprecated `poetry lock --check` continues to fail for an outdated lockfile, but now uses the same clearer stale-lock explanation after its deprecation notice.
Install flows that would consume an existing stale `poetry.lock` no longer emit only a warning; they fail immediately by raising `ValueError` instead of proceeding with dependency installation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project with a present but outdated `poetry.lock`, when `poetry check --lock` is run, it should fail and tell the user that the lock file must be regenerated because `pyproject.toml` changed after the lock was created.
Given a project with a present but outdated `poetry.lock`, when `poetry lock --check` is run, it should still show its deprecation notice and then fail with the same stale-lock guidance.
Given an install operation that would use an outdated existing lockfile, when installation begins, it should stop with an error instead of warning and continuing.
Given a project whose `poetry.lock` is present and current, when lock-based checks or install flows run, they should continue to succeed as they did previously.

task_26.title: Fix poetry shell activation for MSYS2 Python on Windows
task_26.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes a Windows-specific `poetry shell` activation failure for environments created with Python installed via MSYS2. The shell activation logic now recognizes Windows virtual environments that use a POSIX-style `bin` directory instead of assuming the standard `Scripts` layout, allowing affected environments to activate without regressing existing layouts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry shell` can activate virtual environments on Windows when the interpreter was installed via MSYS2 and the environment uses a POSIX-style layout instead of the usual Windows `Scripts` directory.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry shell` activates a `VirtualEnv` on Windows, it should resolve the activation script from the environment's `Scripts` directory when that directory exists, and otherwise fall back to the `bin` directory used by POSIX-like virtual environments created by MSYS2-installed Python. This should prevent activation failures caused by assuming only the Windows `Scripts` layout.
expectation.conceptual: `poetry shell` should work on Windows for both standard Windows virtual environments and MSYS2-style environments by finding the activation script in the layout the environment actually uses.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing behavior for standard Windows virtual environments that provide `Scripts`, and do not change non-Windows activation behavior, which should continue to use `bin`. The fix should be limited to activation-path selection and should not require a different user command or environment format.
constraints.conceptual: The update should add compatibility for the alternate virtual-environment layout without breaking activation for existing environments on Windows or other platforms.

behavior: On Windows, `poetry shell` should prefer the virtual environment's `Scripts` directory for activation when that directory exists.
On Windows, if the virtual environment does not contain `Scripts` and instead uses a POSIX-style `bin` directory, `poetry shell` should use `bin` to locate the activation script.
Virtual environments created from MSYS2-installed Python on Windows should activate successfully through `poetry shell` instead of failing because only `Scripts` was assumed.
On non-Windows platforms, activation should continue to use the `bin` directory as before.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry shell` on Windows against a standard virtual environment that contains `Scripts`, it should activate the environment successfully using that layout.

When a user runs `poetry shell` on Windows against a virtual environment created by MSYS2-installed Python that exposes the activation script under `bin` and not `Scripts`, it should activate the environment successfully.

When `poetry shell` resolves the activation script path, it should base the choice between `Scripts` and `bin` on the actual virtual-environment layout rather than assuming a single Windows convention.
When `poetry shell` is used on non-Windows systems, activation behavior should remain unchanged.

task_28.title: Handle missing project names without confusing validation failures
task_28.description: Poetry now tolerates project configurations that omit the project name during validation so users receive the actual invalid-configuration error instead of a confusing secondary failure. The existing validation that rejects a project name matching one of its dependencies still applies when a name is provided.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry handles project configurations with a missing `name` by surfacing a clear invalid-configuration error, while preserving the existing validation that rejects a project name that duplicates one of its dependencies.

expectation.grounded: During Poetry project validation and project creation, the project-name-versus-dependency-name check should run only when the configuration contains a `name`. If `name` is absent, validation should continue and report the missing-name configuration error instead of failing while comparing the project name against dependencies. If `name` is present, Poetry should still add a validation error when the normalized project name matches a normalized dependency name.
expectation.conceptual: Users who omit the project name should see a normal, understandable configuration error about the missing required field. Users who do define a project name should continue to be prevented from using the same name as one of their dependencies.

constraints.grounded: Do not treat a missing `name` as a valid project configuration, and do not remove the existing project-name conflict validation for configurations that include `name`. The change should only prevent the follow-on failure caused by attempting the comparison when no project name exists.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve error clarity for incomplete project metadata without weakening existing validation rules or changing outcomes for named projects whose metadata is otherwise valid.

behavior: Validation skips the project-name-versus-dependency-name comparison when the project configuration has no `name`.
A configuration missing `name` remains invalid, but the reported failure is the underlying missing-name validation issue rather than an incomprehensible secondary error.
When `name` is present, Poetry still rejects configurations where the project name and any dependency name are equivalent after normalization.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project configuration with no `name`, when Poetry validates or loads the project, it should report an invalid configuration due to the missing project name and should not fail in the project-name-versus-dependency-name check.
Given a project configuration with a `name` that matches a dependency name after normalization, when Poetry validates the project, it should report that name conflict as a validation error.
Given a project configuration with a defined `name` that does not conflict with dependencies, when Poetry validates the project, this change should not add any new name-conflict error.

task_29.title: Support installing local sdist path dependencies
task_29.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes a bug where a dependency added from a local source distribution archive could fail during dependency resolution even though the same archive worked when installed from a URL. Local sdist archives are now preserved as file-based sources during metadata inspection so resolution and installation use the original archive path consistently.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that adding or installing a dependency from a local source distribution archive path works reliably and is handled the same way as the same archive provided by URL, without failing because the package is treated as a directory source.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry inspects a local sdist archive, the resulting package metadata should preserve the original dependency source as a file source that points to the resolved archive path. Adding a dependency from a local archive path should therefore resolve and install it as a file-based dependency rather than as an unpacked directory source.
expectation.conceptual: A dependency supplied as a local source archive should behave like a file dependency, not like a directory dependency. Users should be able to add the archive from disk and get the same successful install behavior they would get from the same archive hosted at a URL.

constraints.grounded: The fix should only affect local sdist archive handling during metadata inspection and resolution. Poetry must not replace the dependency's effective source with a temporary extraction directory or introduce resolver failures that stem solely from that source rewrite.
constraints.conceptual: Only local source archives should change behavior. Real directory dependencies and other source types should keep their existing semantics, and archive inspection should remain transparent to the user.

behavior: Local sdist archives are represented to dependency resolution as file-backed sources associated with the original resolved archive path.
Metadata extraction from an unpacked sdist must not cause the dependency to be reclassified as a directory source.
Installing or adding a dependency from a local sdist path succeeds in cases where the same archive already succeeds when referenced by URL.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid local sdist archive path, when a user adds or installs it as a dependency, then Poetry should resolve and install it successfully as a file-based dependency.

Given the same package archive is available both locally and via URL, when each is added as a dependency, then dependency resolution should treat both consistently enough to avoid path-only failures for the local archive.

When Poetry inspects a local sdist by unpacking it to read metadata, then the dependency's externally visible source should still correspond to the original archive file rather than the temporary extraction directory.

task_30.title: Ignore unavailable unrequested extra path dependencies during install
task_30.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes an install-time bug where `poetry install` could abort because an optional local file or directory dependency inside an extra was unavailable even when that extra was not requested. The upgrade should allow normal installs to proceed for skipped extras while preserving failure when the extra is explicitly selected.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry install` does not fail solely because an optional file or directory dependency belongs to an unrequested extra and is unavailable, while still failing when that extra is explicitly selected.

expectation.grounded: During `poetry install`, optional dependencies represented as `PathDependency` instances and attached to extras that are not requested may be skipped and must not raise `ValueError` during validation. If the same optional file or directory dependency becomes selected through `--extras`, or if any non-skipped file or directory dependency is unavailable, installation should still surface the validation failure.
expectation.conceptual: Installing a project without selecting a given extra should ignore installability problems that exist only inside that unused extra. Selecting the extra should keep the current strict behavior and fail if one of its local file or directory dependencies cannot be resolved.

constraints.grounded: Keep validation for non-skipped file and directory dependencies unchanged. Do not convert unavailable requested extras into silent success, and do not treat skipped optional extras as installed.
constraints.conceptual: Only unused optional extras should stop blocking installation. Requested dependencies must still be validated normally, and the upgrade must not blur the distinction between skipped dependencies and dependencies the user asked to install.

behavior: `poetry install` no longer aborts when an unavailable optional path or directory dependency belongs only to an extra that was not requested.
When the user requests that extra with `--extras`, the same unavailable path or directory dependency still causes installation to fail with the existing validation error signal.
Validation behavior for selected local file and directory dependencies remains strict and unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a project defines an optional local path or directory dependency only through an extra, running `poetry install` without that extra should complete without failing because that dependency is missing or inaccessible.
When the same project is installed with the corresponding `--extras` selection, installation should fail if the extra's local path or directory dependency does not exist or cannot be accessed.
When a local file or directory dependency is part of the requested install set, Poetry should continue to report the validation failure instead of skipping it.

task_32.title: Accept Unicode author names in poetry init
task_32.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes author-field validation in `poetry init` so names containing accented or otherwise canonically equivalent Unicode characters are accepted when they otherwise match the normal author format, instead of being rejected as invalid.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry init` accepts author entries containing accented or other Unicode characters, including canonically equivalent combining-character forms, whenever the entry otherwise matches the existing author-field format.

expectation.grounded: `poetry init` should normalize author prompt input before applying its author-format validation so canonically equivalent Unicode spellings, including precomposed and combining-character accented names, are treated the same. Author input that still violates the existing author syntax should remain invalid, and the current `n`/`no` skip responses should continue to produce no author value.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to enter author names with accented and other Unicode characters in `poetry init` without false validation failures. Different Unicode encodings of the same visible name should behave identically, while genuinely malformed author entries should still be rejected.

constraints.grounded: Do not broaden accepted author syntax beyond the existing `poetry init` author validation rules; only canonical Unicode representation differences should stop causing false negatives. Preserve the existing skip behavior for `n` and `no`.
constraints.conceptual: Improve character handling without loosening the overall author-field contract or changing how users skip the prompt.

behavior: `poetry init` author validation treats canonically equivalent Unicode representations of the same author text as equivalent.
Author names containing accented letters entered through combining-character sequences are accepted when the overall author entry is otherwise valid.
Author names already entered in precomposed Unicode form continue to be accepted under the same validation rules.
Inputs that do not match the existing author entry structure remain invalid, and entering `n` or `no` still skips the author field.
acceptance_criteria: When a user enters an author value in `poetry init` that contains accented characters in decomposed Unicode form, the command should accept it if the entry otherwise follows the expected author format.
When the same author value is entered using precomposed Unicode characters, `poetry init` should behave the same as it does for the decomposed form.
When a user enters `n` or `no` at the author prompt, `poetry init` should still skip author collection.
When an author value is structurally invalid apart from Unicode normalization, `poetry init` should still reject it.

task_31.title: Remove unrequested extras during synchronized installs
task_31.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes synchronized installs so that optional dependencies brought in by previously selected extras are removed when those extras are no longer requested, keeping `poetry install --sync` aligned with the requested environment state.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry install --sync` removes previously installed packages that belong only to extras that are not requested for the current install, so synchronized installs do not leave stale extra dependencies behind.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry install --sync` builds and executes the lockfile-based install plan, uninstall operations associated with omitted extras must be preserved and applied alongside the rest of the operation set. If an extra was installed earlier but is not requested for the current synchronized install, packages that are present only because of that extra should be removed.
expectation.conceptual: A synchronized install should fully match the extras the user asks for. If an optional extra is no longer requested, its packages should be removed instead of remaining in the environment.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the handling of packages required by the base dependency set or by explicitly requested extras. Only packages represented by uninstall operations for omitted extras should be removed, and the normal install/update behavior outside this stale-extra cleanup should remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: Only stale optional extra dependencies should be cleaned up. Packages that are still required by the current project configuration must remain installed, and ordinary install behavior should not regress.

behavior: `poetry install --sync` now retains and executes uninstall operations for dependencies tied to extras that are not requested in the current install.
If the environment already contains packages installed only for an extra that is now omitted, synchronized installation removes those packages instead of leaving them installed.
Dependencies required by the base project or by extras that are still requested remain installed.
The resulting environment after a synchronized install matches the currently requested extras set rather than preserving stale optional dependencies from earlier installs.
acceptance_criteria: When a project previously installed an extra and the user later runs `poetry install --sync` without requesting that extra, packages needed only for the omitted extra should be removed from the environment.
When the user runs `poetry install --sync` and continues to request an extra, the packages for that extra should remain installed.
When stale extra packages are removed during a synchronized install, dependencies still required by the base project or by still-requested extras should remain present.
After `poetry install --sync` completes, the environment should reflect the current requested extras set and should not retain stale optional extra packages.

task_34.title: Support build-requirement CLIs during sdist metadata inspection
task_34.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes metadata extraction for source distributions whose build process invokes command-line tools supplied by declared build requirements, so dependency metadata can be determined in cases that previously failed during isolated build inspection.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry can determine metadata for source distributions when the package's metadata generation step invokes CLI tools provided by its declared build requirements.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry inspects an sdist and builds metadata through its isolated build environment, subprocess calls made during metadata generation must be able to resolve executables installed from the package's build-system requirements. For affected packages, metadata inspection should succeed and return the package metadata instead of failing solely because those build-time CLI tools are not available to the inspection process.
expectation.conceptual: Packages that need build-time command-line tools to compute their metadata should install and resolve normally as long as those tools are declared as build requirements. Poetry should treat those tools as available during metadata extraction and should no longer fail just because they are not on the user's ambient shell PATH.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve isolated metadata inspection behavior, rely only on tools provided by the package's declared build requirements, and avoid changing the metadata contract for packages that do not depend on such CLI invocations. Build failures unrelated to availability of declared build-requirement executables may still surface as metadata inspection errors.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only remove the false failure caused by missing access to declared build-time tools. It should not relax isolation, invent undeclared tool dependencies, or alter successful metadata results for unaffected packages.

behavior: During sdist metadata extraction, CLI executables installed as part of the package's declared build requirements are available to commands launched by the build backend.
Poetry can successfully determine package metadata for sdists whose metadata generation shells out to a declared build-time executable.
Failures caused only by the inspection process not seeing those declared CLI tools are eliminated, while unrelated build or metadata errors can still be reported.
acceptance_criteria: Given a source distribution whose metadata generation invokes a command-line executable supplied by its declared build requirements, when Poetry inspects the package metadata, it should complete successfully and return the package metadata.

When the required executable is available only through the package's declared build requirements and not through the user's outer shell environment, Poetry should still resolve that executable during metadata extraction.
When a package does not depend on build-time CLI invocations for metadata generation, its metadata inspection behavior and resulting metadata should remain unchanged.
When metadata generation fails for reasons other than access to declared build-requirement executables, Poetry may still surface a metadata inspection or build failure.

task_33.title: Handle misconfigured gzip-encoded sdist downloads
task_33.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adjusts source distribution downloads so package servers that incorrectly send archive files with HTTP gzip content encoding no longer cause the downloaded artifact to be transparently decompressed and rejected. This preserves the published archive bytes during installation and avoids failures against misconfigured indexes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry can download and install source distributions from package servers that are misconfigured to send archive responses with HTTP gzip content encoding, without corrupting the saved archive or failing package validation because the downloaded bytes were transformed in transit.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry fetches an sdist over HTTP, it should request identity content encoding so the response is stored as the original archive bytes rather than being transparently decompressed by the HTTP client. As a result, sdist archives such as `.tar.gz` served with an incorrect `Content-Encoding: gzip` header should remain usable for normal hash validation and installation instead of being downloaded in an altered form.
expectation.conceptual: Downloading a source distribution should preserve the exact archive that the package repository publishes, even when the repository is misconfigured. After upgrading to 1.8.0, users should be able to install dependencies from such servers without unexpected hash mismatches or unusable archives caused by HTTP auto-decompression.

constraints.grounded: The change should be limited to HTTP download negotiation for sdist retrieval. Poetry should continue streaming downloads, surface the same HTTP failures for unsuccessful responses, and keep existing behavior for correctly configured servers that already return raw archive bytes.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only prevent download-time content transformation. Existing successful installs from normal package servers should keep working the same way, and ordinary network or server errors should still be reported normally.

behavior: Poetry now asks HTTP servers to return source distribution downloads without content encoding.
A package server that incorrectly serves an sdist archive with `Content-Encoding: gzip` no longer causes the HTTP client to transparently inflate the file before Poetry writes it to disk.
The downloaded artifact retains the original archive bytes expected by downstream validation and installation flow.
Users installing packages from misconfigured indexes should no longer fail because the downloaded sdist content differs from the published archive.
acceptance_criteria: When an sdist is hosted on a package server that incorrectly marks the archive response with HTTP gzip content encoding, Poetry should still download a valid archive file and proceed with installation.
When Poetry downloads a `.tar.gz` sdist from such a server, the file written locally should match the published archive bytes rather than an auto-decompressed variant.
When the package server is correctly configured, Poetry should continue downloading and installing the sdist without a change in observable behavior.
When the HTTP response is unsuccessful, Poetry should still fail through its normal HTTP error handling rather than masking the network problem.

task_35.title: Clear stale environment state after `poetry env remove --all`
task_35.description: Poetry should forget the project's previously selected virtual environment when all managed environments are removed, so stale environment metadata does not survive `poetry env remove --all` and block use of an already activated environment.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry env remove --all` also clears Poetry's remembered environment selection for the current project, so stale metadata from deleted or manually removed virtual environments does not prevent Poetry from using the currently activated environment.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry env remove --all` is executed, Poetry should delete all managed virtual environments it finds and also remove the current project's persisted environment entry from the environment registry when one exists. After that cleanup, Poetry must no longer treat the removed environment as the selected environment for the project and should be able to resolve against the currently activated environment instead of stale registry state.
expectation.conceptual: Removing all project environments should also reset Poetry's saved environment choice for that project. Once the old environments are gone, Poetry should not keep behaving as if a deleted environment is still selected, and an already activated environment should be usable again.

constraints.grounded: Cleanup should be limited to the current project's stored environment selection, should be safe when no environment registry file exists, and should still clear stale project metadata even if the referenced virtual environment was already deleted outside Poetry before the command ran.
constraints.conceptual: The reset should only affect the project whose environments are being removed, must not fail when there is no saved environment state, and must handle previously deleted environments without leaving stale selection data behind.

behavior: Running `poetry env remove --all` now clears the current project's persisted environment selection in addition to deleting discovered virtual environments.
The persisted selection is cleared even if it points to a virtual environment that had already been removed manually and therefore is not deleted during the command's environment-removal loop.
If Poetry has no persisted environment registry for the project, the command still succeeds without extra cleanup work.
acceptance_criteria: When a project has a saved selected environment and the user runs `poetry env remove --all`, Poetry should no longer remember that removed environment for subsequent environment resolution.
When the saved selected environment points to a virtual environment that was already deleted outside Poetry, running `poetry env remove --all` should still clear the stale selection state.

After all project environments have been removed, if the user has a compatible environment already activated, Poetry should be able to use that active environment instead of acting as though the deleted project environment is still selected.
When no saved environment state exists for the project, `poetry env remove --all` should still complete successfully.

task_36.title: Fix poetry shell activation for zsh virtualenv paths with spaces
task_36.description: The update ensures that `poetry shell` can activate a Poetry-managed virtual environment in `zsh` even when the environment path contains spaces. It also aligns shell startup behavior so shells that already perform activation during launch are not given a redundant follow-up activation command.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry shell` reliably opens an activated shell session when the virtual environment path contains spaces, especially for `zsh`, without changing expected activation behavior for other supported shells.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry shell` is run under `zsh`, it should successfully activate the target virtual environment even if `env.path` or the activation script path contains space characters. Shell dispatch should continue to use shell-specific activation behavior: `xonsh` activates through `vox activate`, `nu` and `fish` should rely on activation already performed during shell startup, and other shells should still receive the normal activation command.
expectation.conceptual: `poetry shell` should work the same for users regardless of whether their project or virtual environment lives in a path with spaces. Opening a shell should result in an active environment, and shell-specific startup flows should not trigger duplicate or broken activation steps.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve existing shell-specific behavior outside the path-with-spaces fix: `zsh` still activates through its bash-emulation path, `xonsh` still uses its dedicated activation mechanism, and `nu` and `fish` must not be sent an extra activation command after launch. No regression should be introduced for environments whose paths do not contain spaces.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to making shell activation robust and should not alter the expected startup experience for unaffected shells or normal path layouts. Users who already had working shell activation should continue to see the same outcome.

behavior: Running `poetry shell` in `zsh` with a virtual environment path that includes spaces should no longer fail during activation.
The `zsh` activation flow should treat the activation command as a single shell argument so whitespace in the activation script path does not break command parsing.
For `fish` and `nu`, `poetry shell` should not send an additional activation command after the shell has already been launched with activation handling.
For other supported shells, `poetry shell` should continue using the existing activation command flow.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry shell` from `zsh` and the target virtual environment path contains spaces, the shell session should open with the Poetry environment activated instead of failing to activate.
When a user runs `poetry shell` from `zsh` and the target virtual environment path does not contain spaces, activation behavior should remain successful and unchanged.
When a user runs `poetry shell` from `fish` or `nu`, the session should rely on its startup activation path and should not perform a second visible activation step after launch.
When a user runs `poetry shell` from other supported shells, activation should continue to work through the normal shell-specific command flow.

task_37.title: Fix console script installation for scripts with extras
task_37.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes installation-time generation of console script wrappers when a project script declaration includes extras. Installed commands should resolve and run the declared function normally instead of treating bracketed extras as part of the callable target, and malformed script targets should now fail with clearer validation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that console scripts declared with extras install successfully and invoke the intended callable. Ensure that malformed script declarations are rejected clearly instead of producing unusable installed commands.

expectation.grounded: `poetry install` must correctly handle console script entry points whose target includes bracketed extras metadata. During installed script generation, Poetry should resolve the executable target from the `module:function` portion only, so the generated command invokes the declared callable and does not incorporate extras into the callable name. If a console script target cannot be parsed into exactly one module and one callable, installation should raise `ValueError`; missing callable targets should be reported as invalid function references, and targets with multiple `:` separators should be rejected explicitly.
expectation.conceptual: When a package defines a CLI script with optional extras, installing the project should still create a working command that runs the same function as the script definition without extras. If the script target format itself is invalid, installation should stop with a clear error rather than create a broken command.

constraints.grounded: Valid console script declarations without extras must continue to install unchanged. Extras metadata may be present on a script declaration, but it must not affect module or callable resolution for the installed launcher. Invalid targets must fail during installation instead of being partially accepted or converted into a launcher that points at a non-existent callable.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing working script installation behavior intact, ignore extras for command target resolution, and prefer an explicit install-time failure over silently generating an unusable executable.

behavior: Console script entry points that include bracketed extras metadata are accepted during installation.
The installed launcher resolves and calls the referenced `module:function` target without appending extras to the callable name.
Script targets that omit the callable separator are rejected with `ValueError` instead of producing an installed command.
Script targets that contain more than one callable separator are rejected with `ValueError` instead of being interpreted ambiguously.
acceptance_criteria: When a project defines a script with extras and runs `poetry install`, it should install the command successfully and the installed command should invoke the declared function.
When a script definition includes extras, the installed command should behave the same as the equivalent script target without extras in its callable reference.
When a script target omits the callable portion after the module reference, installation should fail with `ValueError` rather than producing a launcher.
When a script target contains multiple `:` separators, installation should fail with `ValueError` rather than guessing which callable to use.

task_38.title: Preserve explicit sources across dependency extras
task_38.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes dependency resolution so an explicitly configured package source is preserved when the same package is encountered again through dependencies that request no extras or different extras. This prevents incorrect fallback to another repository and keeps extra selection intact during resolution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution preserves an explicitly configured source for a package even when the same package is encountered transitively with no extras or with a different set of extras, so installs and updates continue to pull that package from the intended repository.

expectation.grounded: For dependencies that refer to the same package name and the same source metadata, Poetry's solver should propagate the explicit `source` selection independently of whether a particular occurrence is declared as `name`, `name[extra]`, or `name[other-extra]`. When a dependency with extras reuses previously discovered candidates for the same package, the resolved dependency must still reflect the requested extras while retaining the explicit source information associated with that package selection.
expectation.conceptual: If a project pins a package to an explicit repository, that repository choice should remain in effect for every resolved occurrence of the package, even when some dependency paths request the package without extras or with different extras. The selected extras should still be honored.

constraints.grounded: Reuse and source propagation must stay scoped to dependencies that share the same package name and identical source identity; packages from different explicit sources or source coordinates must remain distinct. The fix must not strip requested extras from the resolved dependency view or alter behavior for dependencies that do not rely on extras-based source propagation.
constraints.conceptual: The change must prevent loss of repository selection without merging unrelated sources or changing which extras are active for the resolved package.

behavior: A direct dependency declared with extras and an explicit source now causes transitive resolutions of the same package without extras to use that explicit source instead of falling back to the default source.
The same source propagation applies when another dependency path requests the same package with a different extra set.
When cached package candidates are reused for a dependency that includes extras, the resolved dependency still carries the requested extras while preserving the correct source metadata.
Source propagation remains isolated by source identity, so equivalent package names from different explicit sources are not conflated.
acceptance_criteria: When a project depends on `lib[extra]` from an explicit source and another resolved dependency requires `lib` without extras, resolution should select `lib` from the explicit source rather than the default source.

When a project depends on `lib[extra]` from an explicit source and another resolved dependency requires `lib` with a different extra set, resolution should still select `lib` from the explicit source and honor the extra set requested by that dependency.

When the same package name is available from multiple explicit sources under different dependency conditions, the selected package should retain the matching explicit source instead of reusing source information from another repository.
When dependency resolution reuses existing candidates for the same package, the resulting package selection should preserve both the chosen source and the extras requested by the active dependency.

task_39.title: Restore debug logging for builds that use a custom build script
task_39.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes build-time diagnostics for projects that use a custom build script. The upgrade preserves the caller's logging verbosity while creating the isolated build environment, exposes captured build-system installation output in debug mode, and makes third-party multiline log output consistently attributable.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that builds using a custom build script no longer lose verbose or debug diagnostic output while Poetry prepares the build environment, and that third-party log output remains readable and attributable during those builds.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry enters `build_environment()` because `poetry.package.build_script` is present, the build must preserve the active logging verbosity across `EnvManager.build_venv()` and the `virtualenv.cli_run()` call. The build-environment preparation step should continue to emit its preparation notice, and when `io.is_debug()` is true, any captured output returned from `venv.run_pip()` while installing build-system requirements should be written to the user. `IOFormatter` should format non-Poetry records so every emitted line is prefixed with a source tag derived from the package path when available, with a fallback to the record module name, and include the logger name for non-root records.
expectation.conceptual: Verbose builds that rely on a custom build script should keep producing diagnostic output throughout build-environment setup. In debug mode, users should see the underlying build-system installation output, and third-party multiline logs should be clearly labeled so their origin is obvious instead of disappearing or becoming ambiguous.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not lower or reset the existing root logger verbosity during virtual environment creation. Extra pip/build-system installation output should only be surfaced when debug mode is active and output is present. Poetry and poetry-core log records should continue to avoid third-party source prefixes, while third-party records receive consistent per-line prefixing.
constraints.conceptual: The change should improve diagnostics without making normal builds unexpectedly noisy, without altering the caller's chosen logging level, and without reformatting first-party Poetry logs as if they came from external packages.

behavior: Builds that require an isolated build environment because a custom build script is configured preserve the current logging verbosity during virtual environment creation instead of dropping to warning-only output.
The build-environment preparation message is emitted as a normal line-oriented status message rather than transient overwritten output.
When debug verbosity is enabled and build-system dependency installation produces output, that captured pip output is shown to the user during build-environment setup.
When debug verbosity is not enabled, the extra captured pip output is not emitted.
Third-party log records are prefixed on every output line, including multiline output, so each line remains attributable to the originating package or logger.

For third-party logs, the displayed prefix uses the detected package name when it can be inferred from the log record path and otherwise falls back to the module name; non-root loggers include their logger name in that prefix.
acceptance_criteria: When a project build uses a custom build script and Poetry is run with verbose or debug logging, build-environment creation should continue honoring that verbosity instead of suppressing debug-level diagnostics mid-build.
When Poetry installs build-system requirements for such a build in debug mode and pip emits output, the user should see that installation output.
When the same build runs without debug mode, the user should still see the build-environment preparation notice but should not receive the extra captured pip output.
When a third-party component emits multiline logs during the build, every line should carry a consistent source prefix so the output remains attributable.
When Poetry emits its own log records during the same flow, those records should not be labeled with third-party prefixes.
After virtual environment creation starts and completes, the logging configuration requested by the caller should remain in effect for subsequent build output.

task_40.title: Preserve explicit sources for locked dependencies
task_40.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes dependency resolution so packages reused from lock data continue to honor explicit sources declared by the project. This prevents installs and updates from losing the intended repository selection when resolving locked dependencies.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependencies declared with an explicit source keep that source association when Poetry resolves them from locked packages, so installs and updates do not lose the intended repository for direct or transitively reached dependencies.

expectation.grounded: When root dependencies declare a `source`, Poetry should retain that source association during locked-package lookup. If a locked package satisfies a dependency whose name matches a root dependency with an explicit source, the resolved dependency should carry the same explicit source before it is returned for further resolution. This source mapping should be recomputed from the current effective root dependency set after overrides have removed duplicates so the active explicit source remains unambiguous.
expectation.conceptual: A package already pinned in the lock should still be treated as coming from the repository the user explicitly selected. Reusing locked dependency data must not strip away repository intent or cause later resolution steps to behave as if the package came from the default source.

constraints.grounded: Only dependencies that currently have an explicit source in the active root dependency set should receive propagated source information. Locked-package matching should continue to use normal dependency satisfaction rules, dependencies without an explicit source should resolve as before, and explicit source information from an earlier override pass must not leak into unrelated lookups.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should stay limited to preserving explicit repository selection. It should not change compatibility matching, alter behavior for dependencies that do not name a source, or carry stale source choices into a different resolution context.

behavior: Poetry records the explicit source associated with each effective root dependency name when preparing the root dependency set for a locked resolution.
When a dependency is satisfied from the lock, Poetry reapplies the recorded explicit source to that dependency before handing the locked package back to the solver.
Explicit source propagation follows the active root dependency definition after duplicate constraints or overrides have been collapsed to a single effective source per package name.
Source propagation is limited to dependency names with an explicit source and is reset between root-resolution passes so stale source metadata is not reused.
acceptance_criteria: When a project declares a dependency with an explicit source and that package is satisfied from the lock, the resolved dependency should continue to be associated with that explicit source.

When another dependency reaches the same locked package transitively, Poetry should still honor the explicit source declared by the project instead of treating the package as coming from the default repository.
When the project's effective root constraints leave one explicit source for a package name after override or marker resolution, locked-package reuse should follow that active source consistently.
When a dependency has no explicit source, locked-package resolution should behave as before and should not inherit a source from an unrelated package.

task_41.title: Correct Poetry self-environment detection
task_41.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes a runtime environment detection bug present in 1.7.1 so Poetry's own interpreter is no longer mistaken for the system Python when Poetry is installed inside a virtual environment.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry does not falsely identify the interpreter running Poetry itself as the system environment when resolving environments, including installs where Poetry runs inside an ordinary virtual environment.

expectation.grounded: For EnvManager.get_system_env with non-naive resolution, Poetry should represent the active sys.prefix interpreter as a GenericEnv layered on its base prefix, with the current SystemEnv treated as the child environment, rather than sometimes exposing the active interpreter as a bare SystemEnv. This should apply consistently even when Poetry's own environment is not in a special Poetry-managed location.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry inspects the Python interpreter it is running under, it should distinguish Poetry's own virtual environment from the real base or system interpreter instead of classifying that runtime as the system environment.

constraints.grounded: Keep naive system-environment lookup unchanged: requesting EnvManager.get_system_env in naive mode should still return the direct SystemEnv for the active prefix. The fix should only change the non-naive classification path and should preserve normal base-prefix resolution.
constraints.conceptual: The change should remove false positives in system-environment detection without altering the explicit raw-system lookup mode or breaking standard interpreter discovery.

behavior: EnvManager.get_system_env using non-naive resolution now always treats the current interpreter as a wrapped environment over its base prefix instead of conditionally returning a bare system environment based on install context.
Poetry no longer relies on special-case install-location detection to recognize that its own runtime interpreter is inside a virtual environment.
A Poetry installation running from a regular virtualenv is no longer misclassified as the system environment during environment resolution.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry is executed from a virtual environment that is not specially marked or stored in a Poetry-managed location, resolving the non-naive system environment should still identify the active interpreter as a virtual environment layered over its base interpreter, not as the system environment.

When Poetry resolves environments while running from its own virtualenv, the returned environment model should preserve both the active prefix and the underlying base prefix so the runtime is not treated as the system Python.
When callers explicitly request naive system-environment resolution, Poetry should continue to return the direct system view of the active prefix without the additional wrapper behavior.

task_43.title: Honor environment overrides for virtualenv options
task_43.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes configuration resolution for nested virtual environment options so environment variables such as POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_SYSTEM_SITE_PACKAGES are applied when Poetry creates a virtual environment. In 1.7.1, these exported overrides could be silently ignored because grouped option tables were returned without resolving nested environment-backed values.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that environment-variable overrides for virtual environment creation options are honored when Poetry resolves and applies virtualenv option settings, so created environments reflect the user's exported configuration instead of defaulting to stored values.

expectation.grounded: When environment-based configuration is enabled, requesting the `virtualenvs.options` configuration table must resolve each nested option through the normal `Config.get` lookup path instead of returning the raw stored mapping. Exported `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_*` values, including `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_SYSTEM_SITE_PACKAGES`, must be reflected in the effective option set used for virtual environment creation, with normal type processing still applied to resolved values.
expectation.conceptual: Poetry should treat virtual environment option values supplied through environment variables the same way it treats equivalent configured values. Reading or using the virtualenv options as a group must preserve nested overrides so the created environment matches the user's requested behavior.

constraints.grounded: The change must not alter unrelated configuration lookup behavior: direct leaf lookups that already honor environment variables must continue to do so, and any `virtualenvs.options` keys without an environment override must continue to use their configured or default values. Grouped table lookup should remain consistent with resolving each child option individually.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to honoring exported overrides without changing defaults for options the user did not set. Nested settings should behave consistently whether users access one option directly or rely on the full options group during normal Poetry operations.

behavior: When Poetry resolves a configuration table while environment overrides are enabled, nested keys are now resolved individually through standard configuration lookup instead of being returned as an unprocessed raw mapping.
When `virtualenvs.options` is used to drive virtual environment creation, `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_*` environment variables now affect the effective option values.

An exported `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_SYSTEM_SITE_PACKAGES=true` is no longer ignored during virtual environment creation and results in system site packages being enabled for the created environment.
Options within `virtualenvs.options` that are not overridden through the environment continue to come from existing configured or default values.
acceptance_criteria: When a user exports `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_SYSTEM_SITE_PACKAGES=true` before creating or installing a project environment, Poetry should create the virtual environment with system site packages enabled.

When Poetry resolves `virtualenvs.options` as a grouped configuration value, any matching `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_*` environment variables should be reflected in the effective option values used by Poetry.
When only a subset of `virtualenvs.options` environment variables is set, Poetry should apply those overrides and leave all other option values unchanged from their configured or default state.
When a nested virtualenv option is read directly or obtained through the `virtualenvs.options` table, the effective value should be consistent.

task_42.title: Stop Silently Dropping setup.py Dependencies
task_42.description: Poetry 1.8.0 makes dependency inspection for legacy setup.py projects pessimistic. If install_requires or extras_require cannot be read reliably from static setup.py analysis, Poetry should treat that parse as failed so dependency metadata is recovered via build-based inspection or surfaced as an error instead of silently omitting dependencies.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry does not silently ignore dependencies declared in a package's setup.py, and that unreadable dependency declarations are recognized as an inspection failure rather than being treated as missing dependencies.

expectation.grounded: When metadata is read from setup.py, SetupReader should only accept install_requires and extras_require when they resolve to supported static forms: a list of strings, a named variable resolving to such a list, None for no dependencies, or extras_require dictionaries whose keys are strings and whose values resolve to string lists, including through literal dict or dict(...) kwargs containers. If SetupReader encounters unsupported values, unreadable kwargs containers, non-string extra keys, or non-string elements inside dependency lists, it should treat setup.py parsing as unsuccessful so higher-level metadata inspection can fall back to build-generated metadata instead of returning incomplete requires_dist data.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry inspects a legacy setup.py-based project, it should either recover the project's declared dependencies accurately or recognize that static parsing was unreliable and switch to a safer metadata source. It must never behave as though unreadable dependencies simply do not exist.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing successful behavior for supported static setup.py declarations, including empty or None dependency fields and extras dictionaries backed by resolvable string lists. Do not silently drop individual unsupported dependency entries or extras sections while continuing as if parsing succeeded.
constraints.conceptual: Simple, statically declared dependencies should continue to work as before, and packages that truly declare no dependencies should still be treated as dependency-free. The change should only remove silent data loss from unreadable declarations.

behavior: Static setup.py inspection now fails fast when install_requires cannot be resolved to a plain list of strings instead of defaulting to an empty dependency list.
Static setup.py inspection now fails fast when extras_require cannot be resolved to a mapping of string extra names to string dependency lists instead of skipping unreadable extras or values.

A kwargs object passed to setup() is only considered readable for dependency extraction when it is a literal dictionary or a dict(...) call; other unresolved kwargs sources are treated as parse failure.
Lists used for dependency extraction must contain only strings; encountering any non-string element causes the setup.py read to be treated as unsuccessful rather than partially accepted.
acceptance_criteria: When a package declares install_requires as a literal list of requirement strings, Poetry should continue to expose those dependencies in the derived package metadata.

When a package declares extras_require as string-named extras whose values are lists of requirement strings, including through named variables that resolve to those lists, Poetry should continue to expose those extras in derived dependency metadata.

When setup.py dependency declarations use unsupported or dynamic constructs that static inspection cannot resolve reliably, Poetry should not return metadata with missing dependencies; it should treat setup.py parsing as failed and rely on build-generated metadata instead.

When no build-based metadata can be produced for an unreadable setup.py dependency declaration, the package inspection flow should fail explicitly rather than succeeding with silently incomplete dependencies.

task_44.title: Honor boolean Poetry env vars for virtualenv options
task_44.description: Poetry 1.8.0 fixes boolean configuration handling for environment-variable overrides so supported `POETRY_*` flags, especially nested `virtualenvs.options` settings, are normalized and applied during runtime operations such as virtual environment creation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that supported boolean Poetry configuration options provided through `POETRY_*` environment variables are interpreted correctly and actually affect runtime behavior, especially virtual environment creation flags such as system site packages, pip, and setuptools handling.

expectation.grounded: `Config.get()` should normalize environment-derived values for supported boolean keys, including `virtualenvs.create`, `virtualenvs.in-project`, `virtualenvs.options.always-copy`, `virtualenvs.options.no-pip`, `virtualenvs.options.no-setuptools`, `virtualenvs.options.system-site-packages`, `virtualenvs.options.prefer-active-python`, `experimental.system-git-client`, `installer.modern-installation`, `installer.parallel`, `solver.lazy-wheel`, `warnings.export`, and `keyring.enabled`. When the corresponding `POETRY_*` environment variables are set, Poetry should expose boolean values and honor them in downstream behavior such as virtual environment creation.
expectation.conceptual: Boolean configuration flags set via environment variables should behave the same way as the equivalent settings in Poetry's normal configuration sources. Users should be able to turn supported features on or off with `POETRY_*` variables and see those choices reflected in actual Poetry behavior.

constraints.grounded: The change should be limited to boolean normalization for supported config keys. Non-boolean settings and unrelated config lookup behavior should remain unchanged, and supported boolean env var overrides should not be ignored or left as string values when consumed by runtime features.
constraints.conceptual: Fix the boolean env var handling without changing unrelated configuration semantics. The update should only make supported boolean overrides reliable and consistent.

behavior: Setting `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_SYSTEM_SITE_PACKAGES` to a boolean value should cause Poetry-created virtual environments to reflect the requested inclusion or exclusion of system site packages.

Setting `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_NO_PIP` or `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_NO_SETUPTOOLS` to a boolean value should be interpreted as a real boolean config override and applied to virtual environment creation behavior.

Supported boolean `POETRY_*` overrides for other affected config keys, such as `solver.lazy-wheel` and `keyring.enabled`, should be normalized consistently instead of remaining raw environment strings.
Boolean overrides supplied through environment variables should be retrievable through configuration lookup with the same boolean meaning as persisted config values.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sets a supported boolean `POETRY_*` environment variable to enable a feature, Poetry should treat that setting as enabled during normal execution.
When a user sets `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_SYSTEM_SITE_PACKAGES=true` before creating a project virtual environment, the created environment should include system site packages.

When a user sets `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_NO_PIP` or `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_OPTIONS_NO_SETUPTOOLS` to `true` or `false`, Poetry should honor the requested enabled or disabled state instead of ignoring the override.
When supported boolean config values are sourced from environment variables, configuration consumers should observe boolean semantics rather than raw string values.

task_45.title: Update deprecated Poetry dev-exclusion guidance
task_45.description: The 1.8.0 update clarifies that the deprecated Poetry `--no-dev` flag should no longer be the recommended user-facing guidance. Documentation and upgrade messaging should direct users to the supported `--without dev` option instead, and the provided code diff does not indicate any accompanying runtime change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that user-facing guidance for installing without development dependencies uses the supported `--without dev` option instead of the deprecated `--no-dev` flag.

expectation.grounded: Poetry documentation, FAQs, examples, and upgrade guidance that describe excluding the `dev` dependency group during install should refer to the `--without dev` option. The deprecated `--no-dev` flag should not be presented as the recommended current usage. No production code change is evidenced for this release note item.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be directed to the current supported way to omit development dependencies, while deprecated syntax is treated as legacy guidance rather than the normal recommended command.

constraints.grounded: Do not describe this update as introducing new install semantics, dependency resolution changes, compatibility changes, or new runtime errors; the provided code diff shows no production behavior change tied to this release note entry.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the scope limited to correcting upgrade and usage guidance about the supported option for excluding development dependencies, without implying a new runtime feature or behavior change.

behavior: The update changes the recommended user-facing syntax for excluding the `dev` dependency group from the deprecated `--no-dev` flag to the supported `--without dev` option.
No production code path, public API behavior, or runtime CLI semantic change is evidenced by the provided code diff for this release-note item.
acceptance_criteria: When user-facing install guidance describes omitting development dependencies, it should reference the `--without dev` option.
When users consult upgrade notes, FAQs, or examples after this update, `--no-dev` should not appear as the recommended syntax for excluding development dependencies.
The upgrade description should make clear that this item is a documentation-level correction and should not claim a new runtime feature or breaking behavior.

task_46.title: Replace deprecated poetry-lock hook guidance with poetry-check
task_46.description: Poetry 1.8.0 changes pre-commit guidance to recommend the supported `poetry-check` hook instead of the deprecated `poetry-lock` hook. The provided artifacts indicate a documentation and upgrade-guidance change rather than a runtime library behavior change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects upgrading to Poetry 1.8.0 use `poetry-check` as the recommended pre-commit hook and stop relying on the deprecated `poetry-lock` hook in user-facing guidance and configuration expectations.

expectation.grounded: For Poetry 1.8.0, pre-commit integrations should treat `poetry-check` as the recommended hook and `poetry-lock` as deprecated. Upgrade guidance should direct users toward `poetry-check` and should no longer present `poetry-lock` as the preferred Poetry pre-commit hook.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, users setting up or maintaining Poetry pre-commit workflows should be pointed to the current supported hook instead of the deprecated one, so new and existing setups follow the intended validation path.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce or imply additional runtime, lockfile-generation, or command-behavior changes beyond the visible deprecation of `poetry-lock` and recommendation of `poetry-check`. Do not include test-related changes or testing instructions.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the upgrade scoped to the pre-commit recommendation change only. It should not promise unrelated behavior changes or require any testing-specific work.

behavior: Poetry 1.8.0 recommends `poetry-check` instead of `poetry-lock` for pre-commit usage.
The `poetry-lock` pre-commit hook is treated as deprecated and should no longer be the recommended choice in upgrade-facing guidance.
The provided artifacts indicate a documentation and configuration-guidance update rather than a new runtime behavior in Poetry itself.
acceptance_criteria: When describing or configuring Poetry 1.8.0 pre-commit usage, it should reference `poetry-check` as the recommended hook.
When an existing pre-commit workflow still uses `poetry-lock`, the upgrade requirement should treat that hook as deprecated rather than as the preferred setup.
The upgrade note should remain limited to the pre-commit hook recommendation change and should not claim unrelated runtime changes.

task_48.title: Document parallel installation of multiple Poetry versions
task_48.description: Poetry 1.8.0 adds user-facing guidance for installing multiple Poetry versions side by side. The provided release note describes installation advice for parallel versions, and the provided code diff shows no runtime source changes, so the update is informational rather than behavioral.
