behavior: The documented meaning of the `develop` attribute is limited to Poetry-specific behavior.
Other tools are not part of the supported contract for `develop` and should not be expected to receive or act on that setting.
The 1.8.0 change is documentation-only and does not introduce a runtime or API behavior change.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the 1.8.0 upgrade guidance, it should be clear that `develop` is a Poetry-specific dependency attribute.
When a project using `develop` is consumed by non-Poetry tooling, the requirement should not claim that those tools will preserve or honor that setting.
When communicating the 1.7.1 to 1.8.0 upgrade, the change should be described as a clarification of interoperability expectations, not as a new functional behavior.

task_62.title: Clarify required inputs for supplemental and secondary sources
task_62.description: Poetry 1.8.0 corrects the guidance for adding supplemental and secondary package sources so users understand that the command expects both a source name and a source URL. Because the provided code diff is empty, this update is treated as a documentation clarification rather than a production behavior change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrade guidance for adding supplemental and secondary package sources clearly states that users must provide both a source name and a source URL.

expectation.grounded: Documentation for Poetry's source-add workflow should show that adding supplemental and secondary sources requires two user-supplied values: a source name and a source URL. The provided code diff contains no production changes, so the evidence supports a correction to documented command usage rather than a change to runtime execution.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading should understand that adding either kind of package source is not URL-only; they need to identify the source and supply its address. The update should remove ambiguity in the documented usage contract.

constraints.grounded: Do not describe new runtime semantics, new warnings, or new exceptions for source addition, because no such changes are evidenced in the supplied code diff. Keep the scope limited to correcting the documented argument requirements for supplemental and secondary sources.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this as a documentation clarification only. Preserve existing behavior and focus on correcting what users are told they need to provide.

behavior: Guidance for adding a supplemental source requires both a source name and a source URL.
Guidance for adding a secondary source follows the same requirement rather than implying that a URL alone is sufficient.
No runtime or API behavior change is evidenced by the provided code diff beyond the corrected usage guidance.
acceptance_criteria: When a user consults upgrade guidance for adding a supplemental source, it should state that both a name and a URL are required.
When a user consults upgrade guidance for adding a secondary source, it should state that both a name and a URL are required.
The upgrade description should present this as a clarification of existing command usage, not as a new runtime feature, fix in execution behavior, or breaking change.

task_63.title: Document PyTorch explicit source usage
task_63.description: Version 1.8.0 adds documentation guidance for using PyTorch with an explicit package source. The change improves discoverability for users working with non-default sources and does not introduce runtime or API behavior changes in the provided artifacts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the upgrade documents how to use PyTorch with an explicit package source so users can understand this supported dependency source configuration.

expectation.grounded: The 1.8.0 upgrade should add a PyTorch example for Poetry's explicit source capability. Based on the provided release note and empty code diff, this is a documentation addition that clarifies how PyTorch dependencies can be associated with an explicit source, without introducing a new public API, CLI behavior, warning, or error condition.
expectation.conceptual: Users should have an official example that shows how to configure PyTorch packages when they come from a source that must be selected explicitly, and the upgrade should improve guidance rather than change product behavior.

constraints.grounded: Treat the change as documentation-only: preserve existing explicit source behavior, dependency resolution semantics, and public interfaces. Do not assume new runtime signals or configuration rules beyond the added PyTorch example.
constraints.conceptual: The update should only make the feature easier to understand. Existing source selection and installation behavior should remain the same.

behavior: The upgrade adds user-facing documentation for a PyTorch-specific explicit source scenario.
No observable runtime, API, or dependency resolution behavior change is evidenced by the provided code diff.
The primary user impact is clearer guidance for configuring PyTorch packages from a non-default source.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reviews the upgraded documentation, they should find a PyTorch example that demonstrates explicit source usage.
When users compare version 1.7.1 to 1.8.0, they should understand that PyTorch explicit source usage is documented more clearly.
When existing users upgrade, explicit source behavior should remain unchanged aside from the availability of the new documentation example.

task_64.title: Deprecate Poetry script extras
task_64.description: poetry-core 1.8.0 deprecates script entry points that declare extras. Projects may still validate and build with declared extras for now, but validation and build-time entry-point generation now surface deprecation warnings, and scripts that reference undefined extras remain invalid.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that script entry points that depend on extras are treated as deprecated, with clear warnings during project validation and package build operations, while script entries that name undefined extras continue to be rejected as invalid configuration.

expectation.grounded: If a `tool.poetry.scripts` entry includes an `extras` list, `Factory.validate()` should add a deprecation warning to its reported warnings instead of silently accepting the pattern. During entry-point conversion and artifact generation in the poetry-core build pipeline, the same script configuration should emit a `DeprecationWarning` while still being processed. Validation must continue to report an error when a script references an extra that is not declared in the project's extras.
expectation.conceptual: Packages can still define scripts behind extras in this release, but maintainers should be warned whenever they validate or build such a package because that configuration is deprecated and planned for removal. Truly invalid script-to-extra references should still fail validation.

constraints.grounded: Do not turn defined script extras into an immediate build or validation failure in 1.8.0. Preserve existing entry-point generation for scripts with declared extras, and retain the existing hard error when a referenced extra is missing from the package configuration.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should warn without abruptly breaking currently valid packages, and it should continue to block misconfigured scripts that point to nonexistent extras.

behavior: Project validation now surfaces a deprecation warning for each script specification that declares one or more extras.
Project validation still reports a configuration error when a script's `extras` list contains an extra name that the package does not define.
Build-time entry-point conversion emits a `DeprecationWarning` for scripts that depend on extras instead of handling them silently.

Wheel, sdist, editable wheel, and metadata-generation flows that process script entry points continue to complete for scripts with declared extras, but now expose the deprecation signal during those operations.
acceptance_criteria: When a project defines a script with an `extras` list and every referenced extra is declared by the project, validating the project should succeed and report a deprecation warning for that script.
When a project defines a script with an `extras` list and builds package artifacts or wheel metadata, the operation should still complete and emit a `DeprecationWarning` for that script.
When a project defines a script whose `extras` list contains an extra that is not declared by the project, validation should report that script as invalid.
When a project defines scripts without extras, the release should not introduce new deprecation warnings for those script definitions.

task_66.title: Refresh the supported license list
task_66.description: Version 1.8.0 refreshes the library's supported license catalog so license-related validation and supported-license reporting align with a newer authoritative list.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that license declarations are evaluated against the updated set of supported licenses so users can rely on current license support without false rejections caused by the older 1.7.1 catalog.

expectation.grounded: In 1.8.0, the library should use an updated supported-license list for its public license handling behavior. License values that are present in the refreshed list should be recognized as supported anywhere the library validates, resolves, or exposes supported licenses, and values outside that refreshed list should continue to be treated as unsupported through the library's normal observable behavior.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, the library should consistently recognize the current supported license set anywhere users provide or inspect license information.

constraints.grounded: The evidence only supports a data refresh to the supported-license list. No separate change in license-processing flow, unrelated metadata behavior, or non-license APIs is indicated beyond aligning support decisions with the updated list.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should only change which licenses are considered supported, without changing unrelated package metadata behavior.

behavior: The library's catalog of supported licenses is updated in 1.8.0.
License support decisions should follow the refreshed catalog rather than the 1.7.1 catalog.
Any user-visible lookup or reporting of supported licenses should reflect the refreshed list.
If a license becomes supported in the refreshed catalog, the library should no longer reject it solely because it was absent from the older catalog.
acceptance_criteria: When a user supplies a license that is included in the 1.8.0 supported-license list, the library should recognize it as supported anywhere license support is validated or resolved.
When a user relies on the library's supported-license data, it should reflect the refreshed 1.8.0 list rather than the older 1.7.1 list.
When a user supplies a license that is not supported under the refreshed list, the library should continue to signal it as unsupported through its normal behavior.

task_68.title: Silence benign git output outside repositories
task_68.description: The upgrade removes irrelevant git command output that could appear when git-backed library behavior runs from a directory that is not itself a git repository. Git operations now behave silently on success and continue to signal real failures through process errors instead of exposing subprocess output text.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that git-backed operations no longer print insignificant git errors when the current working directory is not inside a git repository, while still failing normally for real git command errors.

expectation.grounded: Git-backed operations that use the system git runner, including clone and checkout flows, should execute without surfacing underlying git stdout or stderr during normal execution. These operations should complete successfully without returning command output text, and non-zero git exits should still be surfaced as subprocess failures rather than being treated as success.
expectation.conceptual: When the library interacts with git, users should not see irrelevant console noise just because their current directory is outside a repository. Successful operations should be silent, and genuine git failures should still stop the operation and surface as errors.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress successful git-based workflows such as repository clone or revision checkout. Suppressing subprocess output must not suppress failure signaling for non-zero git exits, and the absence of a surrounding git repository must only stop insignificant output, not change the outcome of otherwise valid operations.
constraints.conceptual: Keep normal git-driven features working the same way from a user perspective, except that benign git noise should disappear. Real failures must still be visible as failures.

behavior: Git subprocess output is no longer emitted to the console for system git operations executed by the library.
Running git-backed library behavior from a working directory that is not inside a git repository no longer prints irrelevant git errors caused solely by that directory context.
Successful clone and checkout operations now signal success by completing without returned command text.
If an underlying git command exits with a failure status, the operation still fails instead of being converted into a silent success.
acceptance_criteria: When a git-backed operation is triggered while the current working directory is not inside a git repository, it should not print irrelevant git error output solely because the directory is outside a repository.
When a repository clone initiated through the library succeeds, it should complete without exposing raw git command output as part of the operation result.
When a revision checkout initiated through the library succeeds, it should complete without exposing raw git command output as part of the operation result.
When an underlying git command fails with a non-zero exit status, the library should still surface the failure instead of silently continuing.

task_67.title: Automatically include standard legal files in wheel and sdist artifacts
task_67.description: The 1.8.0 update changes how poetry-core decides which legal and notice files to bundle into build artifacts. In addition to existing LICENSE handling, builds now automatically pick up common legal file names such as AUTHORS, COPYING, NOTICE, both LICENSE and LICENCE spellings, and files under LICENSES across wheel and source distribution outputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that package builds automatically include well-known legal files in both wheel and source distribution outputs, including common license, notice, copying, and authors files.

expectation.grounded: When poetry-core builds an sdist or wheel, it should automatically detect legal files matching the root-level patterns COPYING*, LICEN[SC]E*, AUTHORS*, and NOTICE*, and it should also include files found under LICENSES/. The sdist should contain those legal files in the source archive, and the wheel should place them under the generated .dist-info directory, preserving relative paths for content originating from LICENSES/. Only actual files should be copied into the wheel metadata area; non-file matches should be ignored.
expectation.conceptual: Building a package should automatically bundle the standard legal documents that users commonly expect to ship with Python distributions. The same family of legal files should be recognized consistently across wheel and source builds, including alternate license spellings and suffixed filenames, and wheel builds should keep those files in package metadata rather than mixing them with importable package contents.

constraints.grounded: Existing automatic inclusion of LICENSE-related files must continue to work. The broadened detection should remain limited to the well-known legal filename families and the LICENSES directory tree, and wheel generation should skip matched paths that are not regular files instead of attempting to copy them.
constraints.conceptual: The change should expand legal-file auto-detection without changing unrelated build contents. It should preserve prior license-file support, avoid treating directories as distributable legal documents, and keep legal assets separated from package code in wheel outputs.

behavior: sdist builds now auto-include root-level legal files named like AUTHORS*, COPYING*, LICENSE*, LICENCE*, and NOTICE*.
sdist builds also auto-include files contained in the LICENSES directory tree.
Wheel builds now include the same expanded set of legal files, not just the previously recognized subset.
Wheel metadata places detected legal files under the built .dist-info directory, and nested files from LICENSES/ retain their relative subpaths there.
Filename variants with suffixes are recognized for the supported legal-file families.
Paths matched during legal-file collection that are not regular files are skipped during wheel metadata generation.
acceptance_criteria: When a project root contains files such as AUTHORS, COPYING, NOTICE, LICENSE, LICENCE, or suffix variants like LICENSE.txt, building an sdist should include them automatically in the source archive.
When the same project is built as a wheel, those legal files should be present under the wheel's .dist-info directory rather than alongside importable package modules.

When a project contains files under a LICENSES directory, both sdist and wheel builds should include those files automatically, and the wheel should preserve their relative structure beneath .dist-info.
When a matched legal-file path is a directory rather than a file, wheel creation should ignore that path instead of copying it as a legal file.

When a project relies on the existing automatic handling of LICENSE files, upgrading to 1.8.0 should preserve that behavior while additionally recognizing AUTHORS, NOTICE, COPYING, LICENCE, and LICENSES content.

task_65.title: Allow Path Dependencies Without a Declared Build System
task_65.description: Poetry 1.8.0 removes a false validation barrier for local path dependencies whose pyproject metadata does not include a [build-system] table. Path-based projects that are otherwise valid should still be inspected, resolved, and used without forcing users to add an explicit build-system declaration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that local path dependencies are accepted and resolved even when their pyproject.toml omits a [build-system] section, as long as the project metadata is otherwise valid.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry inspects a directory or path dependency through PackageInfo path inspection, a pyproject.toml that identifies a Poetry project must not be rejected solely because the [build-system] table is missing. PyProjectTOML-based project detection and Factory.create_poetry package loading should continue to produce package metadata such as name, version, Python constraints, dependencies, and extras instead of failing only on the absence of [build-system].
expectation.conceptual: A package referenced by local path should work the same whether or not it explicitly declares a build system in pyproject.toml, provided the project metadata itself is valid. The upgrade should remove failures caused only by the missing build-system table and let dependency metadata be read normally.

constraints.grounded: Do not require [build-system] to exist as a prerequisite for recognizing or inspecting a valid path dependency. Existing behavior for path dependencies that already declare [build-system] must remain unchanged, and invalid project metadata unrelated to the missing build-system table may still fail through the normal error path.
constraints.conceptual: Missing build-system configuration alone must no longer block local dependency usage, but the upgrade should not mask unrelated project metadata errors or change behavior for projects that were already valid.

behavior: A local directory dependency with valid Poetry project metadata is treated as an inspectable project even if pyproject.toml has no [build-system] table.
Dependency inspection for such a path dependency returns package metadata instead of failing solely because the build-system section is absent.
Name, version, Python requirement, declared dependencies, and extras for the path dependency remain discoverable through normal Poetry package loading.
Path dependencies that already include [build-system] continue to resolve with no behavioral regression.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency is declared by local path and its pyproject.toml defines a valid Poetry project but omits [build-system], Poetry should still inspect and resolve that dependency successfully.
When Poetry reads such a path dependency, it should expose the package's declared metadata and dependency requirements rather than failing because the build-system table is missing.
When two otherwise equivalent path dependencies differ only by the presence of [build-system], the one without the table should no longer be rejected for that reason alone.
When a path dependency is invalid for reasons unrelated to [build-system], Poetry may still report the existing failure for those unrelated issues.

task_69.title: Fix Windows Git repository detection and build subprocess decoding
task_69.description: The upgrade fixes an encoding-related regression in build-time Git detection on Windows and hardens subprocess text decoding used during wheel tag discovery. Projects in Git repositories, including repositories whose paths contain non-ASCII characters, should continue to be recognized correctly during packaging, and the affected build subprocesses should no longer rely on ambiguous default text decoding.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that packaging workflows still recognize a Windows project as being inside a Git repository even when the repository path contains non-ASCII characters, and that build-time subprocess output is decoded consistently so encoding-related warnings or path corruption do not interfere with packaging behavior.

expectation.grounded: `poetry.core.vcs.get_vcs()` must correctly interpret the output of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` for Windows repository roots that contain non-ASCII characters and return a `Git` instance instead of behaving as if no VCS were present. As a result, builder flows that depend on VCS detection, including Git-ignored file exclusion, must continue to use repository information. In addition, `WheelBuilder._get_sys_tags()` must decode the subprocess output used for wheel tag discovery without triggering `EncodingWarning` due to unspecified text decoding. Existing failure signaling remains the same: directories that are ignored or not in a repository still yield no VCS, and wheel tag subprocess failures still raise `RuntimeError`.
expectation.conceptual: Build behavior should be the same for repositories in ASCII and non-ASCII paths. On Windows, being inside a Git repository must still be detected reliably during packaging so Git-aware exclusions remain effective, and build steps that query another interpreter for wheel tags should read subprocess text with a stable encoding so they do not emit encoding-related warnings or misread output.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the non-encoding behavior of `get_vcs()`: ignored directories, directories outside a Git repository, missing Git executables, and other Git command failures must still be treated as no VCS. Do not change the error contract of `WheelBuilder._get_sys_tags()`: if the subprocess call fails, it must still surface as `RuntimeError`. Existing successful behavior for ASCII-only paths and unaffected platforms must remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be narrowly scoped to encoding-sensitive repository detection and wheel tag lookup. It must not alter how non-Git directories are classified, introduce fallback behavior that hides subprocess failures, or regress builds that already work.

behavior: `get_vcs()` now treats the Git top-level path returned by `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` as correctly decoded text for Windows repositories whose paths include non-ASCII characters, preventing false loss of Git detection.
When that Git detection succeeds, packaging continues to apply VCS-aware file exclusion instead of behaving as though the project is outside a repository.
`WheelBuilder._get_sys_tags()` now reads subprocess text for wheel tag discovery with an explicit decoding choice, avoiding default-encoding warnings from that subprocess path.
Unrelated control flow remains unchanged: non-repository or ignored directories still resolve to no VCS, and failed sys-tag subprocess calls still raise `RuntimeError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a Windows project is built from inside a Git repository whose absolute path contains non-ASCII characters, the build should still recognize the project as being in Git and honor Git-based ignore handling.
When the project directory is ignored by Git, outside any Git repository, or Git cannot be invoked, the build should continue to behave as non-VCS-managed rather than forcing repository behavior.
When wheel tag resolution queries a target interpreter through a subprocess, it should return the interpreter tags without emitting `EncodingWarning` caused by unspecified subprocess text decoding.
When the subprocess used for wheel tag resolution fails, the build should still fail with `RuntimeError` rather than silently falling back to a different tag source.
